Ctrl + K ) } ``` *** ## API ### `Tooltip.Provider` Wraps your app (or section) to coordinate tooltip delays. When a user moves from one tooltip trigger to another quickly, the second tooltip opens instantly (skip delay). | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `delayDuration` | `number` | `700` | Delay in ms before tooltip opens | | `closeDelay` | `number` | `0` | Delay in ms before tooltip closes once the pointer leaves it | | `skipDelayDuration` | `number` | `300` | Time in ms before delay resets after closing. `0` keeps the delay on every tooltip | | `disableHoverableContent` | `boolean` | `false` | Close immediately when pointer leaves trigger (can't hover content) | ### `Tooltip.Root` Manages state for a single tooltip instance. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `open` | `boolean` | - | Controlled open state | | `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Initial open state | | `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` | - | Called on state change | | `delayDuration` | `number` | - | Override Provider's delay for this tooltip | | `closeDelay` | `number` | - | Override Provider's close delay for this tooltip | | `disableHoverableContent` | `boolean` | - | Override Provider's setting | | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Keeps the tooltip closed, even while a parent holds `open`, closes it if it is open, and drops an open still waiting on its delay | | `dir` | `'ltr' \| 'rtl'` | - | Direction of the content. Without it the content takes the nearest `DirectionProvider`, then ``. The trigger keeps the page's | ### `Tooltip.Trigger` The element that activates the tooltip on hover/focus. While the tooltip is open, the trigger's `aria-describedby` adds the content's id after any ids it was given. Focus opens the tooltip only when the last input was not a pointer press and the trigger matches `:focus-visible`. So a trigger that is also a menu or dialog trigger shows no tooltip when an item chosen with the pointer, or a dialog closed with the pointer, gives focus back to it. Tab, Escape handing focus back, and a focus no input led to, such as a screen reader moving it, open it. A press on the trigger during the open delay drops the open, so the tooltip does not appear after the click. With a trigger nested inside another trigger, the pointer over the inner one opens only its own tooltip. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `disableCloseOnClick` | `boolean` | `false` | When `true`, clicking the trigger does not dismiss the tooltip. Use when wrapping interactive elements like `Toggle` with `asChild`. | When `disableCloseOnClick` is enabled: * The tooltip's `data-slot` and `data-state` are not set on the trigger, so the child element's own attributes pass through unchanged * The tooltip's `onClick` handler is not attached, so the child's `onClick` works without interference * `onPointerDown` skips tooltip close * A `data-tooltip-state` attribute is set instead for tooltip-specific styling if needed * Hover and blur behavior remain unchanged ```tsx import * as Tooltip from '@gentleduck/primitives/tooltip' import { Toggle } from '@gentleduck/primitives/toggle' Bold Toggle bold formatting ``` ### `Tooltip.Portal` Portals content to `document.body`. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `container` | `Element \| DocumentFragment \| RefObject \| null` | `document.body` | Portal target | | `forceMount` | `true` | - | Keep the content mounted while closed | ### `Tooltip.Content` The floating tooltip content. Positioned by the Popper engine. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `aria-label` | `string` | - | Announced in place of the visible content, from a visually hidden `role="tooltip"` element | | `id` | `string` | - | The id the trigger's `aria-describedby` points at. Generated when not given | | `side` | `'top' \| 'right' \| 'bottom' \| 'left'` | `'top'` | Preferred side | | `sideOffset` | `number` | `0` | Distance from anchor in pixels | | `align` | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end'` | `'center'` | Alignment along the side | | `alignOffset` | `number` | `0` | Alignment offset in pixels | | `forceMount` | `true` | - | Keep mounted always | | `onEscapeKeyDown` | `(event) => void` | - | Called on Escape press | | `onPointerDownOutside` | `(event) => void` | - | Called on outside click | It also takes the rest of [Popper](/duck-primitives/api/popper)'s positioning props, with the same defaults: `arrowPadding`, `avoidCollisions`, `collisionBoundary`, `collisionPadding`, `sticky`, `shiftCrossAxis`, `hideWhenDetached` and `updatePositionStrategy`. `updateOnScroll` is always off, since a scroll closes the tooltip. ### `Tooltip.Arrow` Optional visual arrow pointing toward the trigger. *** ## Data attributes }> Content exposes `data-state` with values: `closed`, `delayed-open`, `instant-open`. Use this for different enter animations based on whether the tooltip was delayed or instant. *** ## Accessibility The content is the `role="tooltip"` element and renders its children once. With an `aria-label`, the label moves to a visually hidden element that takes the role and the id instead. Inside a modal `Dialog` but portalled out of it, the content registers with the dialog, so focus can move into it and it scrolls under the dialog's scroll lock. *** ## Grace area When the user moves their pointer from the trigger toward the content, a grace area (triangle) keeps the tooltip open during the transition. This prevents the tooltip from closing when the user moves diagonally to interact with the content. The area is checked from the move that leaves the trigger, so a pointer that lands outside it closes the tooltip at once, and one that lands on another trigger in the same provider opens that tooltip on the same move. Set `disableHoverableContent={true}` to disable this behavior. With `closeDelay`, a pointer leaving the trigger or straying out of the grace area closes the tooltip only after that many milliseconds, and a pointer coming back to the trigger or onto the content keeps it open. A press, a blur, Escape, a scroll or another tooltip opening still closes it at once. *** ## Keyboard interactions | Key | Action | | --- | --- | | Tab | Focus trigger, opens tooltip | | Escape | Close tooltip |

import * as Accordion from '@gentleduck/primitives/accordion'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

const FAQ = [
  {
    value: 'shipping',
    question: 'How long does shipping take?',
    answer: 'Three to five working days in most regions.',
  },
  { value: 'returns', question: 'Can I return an order?', answer: 'Yes, within 30 days, in its original packaging.' },
  { value: 'warranty', question: 'Is there a warranty?', answer: 'Every product carries a two-year warranty.' },
]

export function AccordionSingleExample() {
  return (
    <Accordion.Root className={styles.disclosure} collapsible defaultValue="shipping" type="single">
      {FAQ.map((item) => (
        <Accordion.Item className={styles.disclosureItem} key={item.value} value={item.value}>
          <Accordion.Header className={styles.disclosureHeader}>
            <Accordion.Trigger className={styles.disclosureTrigger}>
              {item.question}
              <Accordion.Indicator className={styles.chevron}>v</Accordion.Indicator>
            </Accordion.Trigger>
          </Accordion.Header>
          <Accordion.Content className={`${styles.disclosureContent} ${styles.animated}`}>
            <div>{item.answer}</div>
          </Accordion.Content>
        </Accordion.Item>
      ))}
    </Accordion.Root>
  )
}

const SECTIONS = ['Account', 'Billing', 'Notifications']

        </Accordion.Item>
      ))}
    </Accordion.Root>
  )
}

import * as Accordion from '@gentleduck/primitives/accordion'
import * as React from 'react'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

const STEPS = ['Details', 'Address', 'Payment']

export function AccordionControlledExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = React.useState('Details')
  const [focused, setFocused] = React.useState<string | null>(null)
  const at = STEPS.indexOf(value)

  return (
    <div className={styles.stack}>
      <Accordion.Root
        className={styles.disclosure}
        onFocusChange={setFocused}
        onValueChange={setValue}
        type="single"
        value={value}>
        {STEPS.map((step) => (
          <Accordion.Item className={styles.disclosureItem} key={step} value={step}>
            <Accordion.Header className={styles.disclosureHeader}>
              <Accordion.Trigger className={styles.disclosureTrigger}>{step}</Accordion.Trigger>
            </Accordion.Header>
            <Accordion.Content className={styles.disclosureContent}>
              <div>Fill in your {step.toLowerCase()}.</div>
            </Accordion.Content>
          </Accordion.Item>
        ))}
      </Accordion.Root>
      <div className={styles.row}>
        <button
          className={styles.button}
          disabled={at <= 0}
          onClick={() => setValue(STEPS[at - 1] ?? '')}
          type="button">
          Back
        </button>
        <button
          className={`${styles.button} ${styles.primary}`}
          disabled={at >= STEPS.length - 1}
          onClick={() => setValue(STEPS[at + 1] ?? '')}
          type="button">
          Next
        </button>
      </div>
      <p className={styles.note}>
        Open: {value || 'none'}. Focused trigger: {focused ?? 'none'}.
      </p>
    </div>
  )
}

import * as Accordion from '@gentleduck/primitives/accordion'
import * as React from 'react'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

export function AccordionDisabledExample() {
  const [locked, setLocked] = React.useState(false)

  return (
    <div className={styles.stack}>
      <Accordion.Root className={styles.disclosure} collapsible disabled={locked} type="single">
        <Accordion.Item className={styles.disclosureItem} value="plan">
          <Accordion.Header className={styles.disclosureHeader}>
            <Accordion.Trigger className={styles.disclosureTrigger}>Plan</Accordion.Trigger>
          </Accordion.Header>
          <Accordion.Content className={styles.disclosureContent}>
            <div>Free plan, renewed monthly.</div>
          </Accordion.Content>
        </Accordion.Item>
        <Accordion.Item className={styles.disclosureItem} disabled value="sso">
          <Accordion.Header className={styles.disclosureHeader}>
            <Accordion.Trigger className={styles.disclosureTrigger}>Single sign-on (Enterprise only)</Accordion.Trigger>
          </Accordion.Header>
          <Accordion.Content className={styles.disclosureContent}>
            <div>Connect your identity provider.</div>
          </Accordion.Content>
        </Accordion.Item>
        <Accordion.Item className={styles.disclosureItem} value="usage">
          <Accordion.Header className={styles.disclosureHeader}>
            <Accordion.Trigger className={styles.disclosureTrigger}>Usage</Accordion.Trigger>
          </Accordion.Header>
          <Accordion.Content className={styles.disclosureContent}>
            <div>1,204 of 5,000 requests this month.</div>
          </Accordion.Content>
        </Accordion.Item>
      </Accordion.Root>
      <button className={styles.button} onClick={() => setLocked((value) => !value)} type="button">
        {locked ? 'Unlock every item' : 'Disable every item'}
      </button>
      <p className={styles.note}>The arrow keys pass over a disabled trigger.</p>
    </div>
  )
}

import * as Accordion from '@gentleduck/primitives/accordion'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

const PANELS = ['Mon', 'Tue', 'Wed', 'Thu']

export function AccordionHorizontalExample() {
  return (
    <div className={styles.stack}>
      <Accordion.Root
        className={styles.disclosure}
        defaultValue="Tue"
        loop={false}
        orientation="horizontal"
        type="single">
        {PANELS.map((day) => (
          <Accordion.Item className={styles.disclosureItem} key={day} value={day}>
            <Accordion.Header className={styles.disclosureHeader}>
              <Accordion.Trigger className={styles.disclosureTrigger}>{day}</Accordion.Trigger>
            </Accordion.Header>
            <Accordion.Content className={styles.disclosureContent}>
              <div>Shifts on {day}</div>
            </Accordion.Content>
          </Accordion.Item>
        ))}
      </Accordion.Root>
      <p className={styles.note}>ArrowLeft and ArrowRight move between days, and stop at either end with loop off.</p>
    </div>
  )
}

import * as Accordion from '@gentleduck/primitives/accordion'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

const ITEMS = [
  { value: 'a', question: 'هل يدعم إمكانية الوصول؟', answer: 'نعم، يتبع نمط WAI-ARIA.' },
  { value: 'b', question: 'هل يأتي بتنسيق جاهز؟', answer: 'لا، التنسيق متروك لك.' },
]

export function AccordionRtlExample() {
  return (
    <div className={styles.stack}>
      <Accordion.Root className={styles.disclosure} collapsible dir="rtl" orientation="horizontal" type="single">
        {ITEMS.map((item) => (
          <Accordion.Item className={styles.disclosureItem} key={item.value} value={item.value}>
            <Accordion.Header className={styles.disclosureHeader}>
              <Accordion.Trigger className={styles.disclosureTrigger}>{item.question}</Accordion.Trigger>
            </Accordion.Header>
            <Accordion.Content className={styles.disclosureContent}>
              <div>{item.answer}</div>
            </Accordion.Content>
          </Accordion.Item>
        ))}
      </Accordion.Root>
      <p className={styles.note}>ArrowLeft moves to the next item, since the items run right to left.</p>
    </div>
  )
}

import * as Accordion from '@gentleduck/primitives/accordion'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

export function AccordionHiddenUntilFoundExample() {
  return (
    <div className={styles.stack}>
      <Accordion.Root className={styles.disclosure} collapsible type="single">
        <Accordion.Item className={styles.disclosureItem} value="rivers">
          <Accordion.Header className={styles.disclosureHeader}>
            <Accordion.Trigger className={styles.disclosureTrigger}>Rivers</Accordion.Trigger>
          </Accordion.Header>
          <Accordion.Content className={styles.disclosureContent} hiddenUntilFound>
            <div>An otter can hold its breath for eight minutes.</div>
          </Accordion.Content>
        </Accordion.Item>
        <Accordion.Item className={styles.disclosureItem} value="forests">
          <Accordion.Header className={styles.disclosureHeader}>
            <Accordion.Trigger className={styles.disclosureTrigger}>Forests</Accordion.Trigger>
          </Accordion.Header>
          <Accordion.Content className={styles.disclosureContent} hiddenUntilFound>
            <div>A red squirrel buries thousands of seeds each autumn.</div>
          </Accordion.Content>
        </Accordion.Item>
      </Accordion.Root>
      <p className={styles.note}>Search the page for "otter" and the browser opens the item that holds it.</p>
    </div>
  )
}

import * as Accordion from '@gentleduck/primitives/accordion'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

export function AccordionForceMountExample() {
  return (
    <Accordion.Root className={styles.disclosure} collapsible type="single">
      {['Summary', 'Details'].map((section) => (
        <Accordion.Item className={styles.disclosureItem} key={section} value={section}>
          <Accordion.Header className={styles.disclosureHeader}>
            <Accordion.Trigger className={styles.disclosureTrigger}>{section}</Accordion.Trigger>
          </Accordion.Header>
          <Accordion.Content className={`${styles.disclosureContent} ${styles.collapse}`} forceMount>
            <div>Kept in the page while closed, so its own styles collapse it.</div>
          </Accordion.Content>
        </Accordion.Item>
      ))}
    </Accordion.Root>
  )
}

import * as Accordion from '@gentleduck/primitives/accordion'
import * as React from 'react'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

export function AccordionItemOpenChangeExample() {
  const [log, setLog] = React.useState<string[]>([])
  const record = (section: string) => (open: boolean) =>
    setLog((entries) => [`${section} ${open ? 'opened' : 'closed'}`, ...entries].slice(0, 4))

  return (
    <div className={styles.stack}>
      <Accordion.Root className={styles.disclosure} collapsible type="single">
        {['Orders', 'Invoices'].map((section) => (
          <Accordion.Item
            className={styles.disclosureItem}
            key={section}
            onOpenChange={record(section)}
            value={section}>
            <Accordion.Header className={styles.disclosureHeader}>
              <Accordion.Trigger className={styles.disclosureTrigger}>{section}</Accordion.Trigger>
            </Accordion.Header>
            <Accordion.Content className={styles.disclosureContent}>
              <div>Recent {section.toLowerCase()}.</div>
            </Accordion.Content>
          </Accordion.Item>
        ))}
      </Accordion.Root>
      <p className={styles.note}>{log.length ? log.join(', ') : 'Open an item to see its own onOpenChange.'}</p>
    </div>
  )
}

import * as NavigationMenu from '@gentleduck/primitives/navigation-menu'
import * as React from 'react'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

export function NavigationMenuControlledExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = React.useState('')

  return (
    <div className={styles.stack}>
      <NavigationMenu.Root className={styles.relative} onValueChange={setValue} value={value}>
        <NavigationMenu.List className={styles.navList}>
          {['Products', 'Pricing'].map((name) => (
            <NavigationMenu.Item key={name} value={name}>
              <NavigationMenu.Trigger className={styles.menubarTrigger}>{name}</NavigationMenu.Trigger>
              <NavigationMenu.Content className={styles.navContent}>
                <NavigationMenu.Link className={styles.navLink} href={`#${name.toLowerCase()}`}>
                  All {name.toLowerCase()}
                </NavigationMenu.Link>
              </NavigationMenu.Content>
            </NavigationMenu.Item>
          ))}
        </NavigationMenu.List>
        <NavigationMenu.Viewport className={styles.viewport} />
      </NavigationMenu.Root>
      <p className={styles.note} style={{ marginTop: '7rem' }}>
        Open item: {value || 'none'}.{' '}
        <button className={styles.button} onClick={() => setValue('Pricing')} type="button">
          Open Pricing
        </button>
      </p>
    </div>
  )
}

          </NavigationMenu.Content>
        </NavigationMenu.Item>
      </NavigationMenu.List>

  )

import * as NavigationMenu from '@gentleduck/primitives/navigation-menu'
import * as React from 'react'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

export function NavigationMenuLinksExample() {
  const [page, setPage] = React.useState('#overview')
  const [filters, setFilters] = React.useState(0)

  return (
    <NavigationMenu.Root className={styles.relative}>
      <NavigationMenu.List className={styles.navList}>
        <NavigationMenu.Item value="pages">
          <NavigationMenu.Trigger className={styles.menubarTrigger}>Pages</NavigationMenu.Trigger>
          <NavigationMenu.Content className={styles.navContent}>
            {['#overview', '#activity', '#billing'].map((href) => (
              <NavigationMenu.Link
                active={href === page}
                className={styles.navLink}
                href={href}
                key={href}
                onSelect={(event) => {
                  event.preventDefault()
                  setPage(href)
                }}>
                {href.slice(1)}
              </NavigationMenu.Link>
            ))}
            <NavigationMenu.Link
              className={styles.navLink}
              closeOnSelect={false}
              href="#"
              onSelect={(event) => {
                event.preventDefault()
                setFilters((count) => count + 1)
              }}>
              Add a filter ({filters}), keeps the menu open
            </NavigationMenu.Link>
          </NavigationMenu.Content>
        </NavigationMenu.Item>
      </NavigationMenu.List>
      <NavigationMenu.Viewport className={styles.viewport} />
    </NavigationMenu.Root>
  )
}

Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `value` | `string` | - | Controlled open item value | | `defaultValue` | `string` | `''` | Initial open item value | | `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | - | Called when open value changes | | `dir` | `'ltr' \| 'rtl'` | - | Text direction. Resolved with `useDirection` (`dir` prop -> `DirectionProvider` -> `'ltr'`). | | `orientation` | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | `'horizontal'` | Menu orientation | | `delayDuration` | `number` | `200` | Delay before an item opens when the pointer rests on its trigger. A click on the trigger before it runs out cancels the open. Ignored in `manual` mode | | `skipDelayDuration` | `number` | `300` | Time window to skip reopen delay. Ignored in `manual` mode | | `closeDelay` | `number` | `150` | How long an item stays open after the pointer leaves it. Ignored in `manual` mode | | `activationMode` | `'automatic' \| 'manual'` | `'automatic'` | `automatic` opens an item when the pointer rests on its trigger and closes it when the pointer leaves; `manual` opens and closes it only on a click | | `...props` | `React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'nav'>` | - | Additional props for root nav | ### `NavigationMenu.Sub` | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `value` | `string` | - | Controlled sub-menu value | | `defaultValue` | `string` | `''` | Initial sub-menu value | | `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | - | Called when sub-menu value changes | | `orientation` | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | `'horizontal'` | Sub-menu orientation | | `activationMode` | `'automatic' \| 'manual'` | the root's | As on the root, for this sub-menu's items | | `disableToggle` | `boolean` | `true` | Keeps an open item open when its trigger is clicked again. `false` closes it | ### `NavigationMenu.List` List wrapper for menu items and indicator tracking. ### `NavigationMenu.Item` | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `value` | `string` | auto-generated | Stable item key used by trigger/content pairing | ### `NavigationMenu.Trigger` Interactive trigger button for an item. Sets `aria-expanded` and `data-state`, and `aria-controls` while its content is open, so it never points at an element that is not rendered. ### `NavigationMenu.Content` Content panel for an item. Supports pointer/focus outside handlers from dismissable layer props. Focus moving outside the menu closes it only when it left from inside the menu, so a dialog that focuses itself on open leaves the menu open. It carries `data-state`, `open` or `closed`, inside the viewport as well as out of it, so a force-mounted content can be hidden while closed. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `forceMount` | `true` | - | Keep mounted for animation control | | `onEscapeKeyDown` | `(event: KeyboardEvent) => void` | - | Called on Escape. Prevent default to keep the item open | | `onPointerDownOutside` | `(event) => void` | - | Called for a press outside the menu | | `onFocusOutside` | `(event) => void` | - | Called when focus moves outside the menu | | `onInteractOutside` | `(event) => void` | - | Called for any outside interaction | It carries `data-slot="navigation-menu-content"`. While its content is closed, its links leave the tab order, and each gets its own `tabindex` back, or none if it had none, when it opens. It finds them as `FocusScope` does, so it skips what is hidden, inert or in a disabled fieldset, and a Tab from a link inside a shadow root moves on through the content. ### `NavigationMenu.Link` Composable link slot used inside content. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `active` | `boolean` | `false` | Marks link as current page (`aria-current="page"`) | | `onSelect` | `(event: Event) => void` | - | Called on link selection before root dismiss | | `closeOnSelect` | `boolean` | `true` | `false` keeps the menu open once the link is selected. A click with Cmd, Ctrl, Shift or Alt held leaves it open either way, since the link opens in another tab or window, or downloads, and the page stays | ### `NavigationMenu.Indicator` Positions an active-item indicator relative to the current trigger. import * as Pagination from '@gentleduck/primitives/pagination'
import * as React from 'react'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

const ITEMS = Array.from({ length: 47 }, (_, index) => `Order #${1000 + index}`)
const PER_PAGE = 5

export function PaginationControlledExample() {
  const [page, setPage] = React.useState(1)
  const shown = ITEMS.slice((page - 1) * PER_PAGE, page * PER_PAGE)

  return (
    <div className={styles.stack}>
      <ul className={styles.note} style={{ margin: 0, paddingInlineStart: '1rem' }}>
        {shown.map((item) => (
          <li key={item}>{item}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
      <Pagination.Root onPageChange={setPage} page={page} pageCount={Math.ceil(ITEMS.length / PER_PAGE)}>
        <Pagination.Content className={styles.pages}>
          <Pagination.Item>
            <Pagination.Previous />
          </Pagination.Item>
          <Pagination.Pages />
          <Pagination.Item>
            <Pagination.Next />
          </Pagination.Item>
        </Pagination.Content>
      </Pagination.Root>
    </div>
  )
}

import * as Pagination from '@gentleduck/primitives/pagination'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

export function PaginationLinksExample() {
  return (
    <div className={styles.stack}>
      <Pagination.Root defaultPage={2} getPageHref={(page) => `?page=${page}`} pageCount={6}>
        <Pagination.Content className={styles.pages}>
          <Pagination.Item>
            <Pagination.Previous />
          </Pagination.Item>
          <Pagination.Pages />
          <Pagination.Item>
            <Pagination.Next rel="next" />
          </Pagination.Item>
          <Pagination.Item>
            <Pagination.Last rel="noopener" target="_blank">
              Last, in a new tab
            </Pagination.Last>
          </Pagination.Item>
        </Pagination.Content>
      </Pagination.Root>
      <p className={styles.note}>
        getPageHref makes every control a link, with a link's own target and rel. One with nowhere to go loses its
        address.
      </p>
    </div>
  )
}

import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

export function PaginationCustomPagesExample() {
  return (
    <Pagination.Root defaultPage={4} pageCount={9}>
      <Pagination.Content className={styles.pages}>
        <Pagination.Pages>
          {(items) =>
            items.map((item) => (
              <Pagination.Item key={item}>
                {typeof item === 'number' ? (
                  <Pagination.Page aria-label={`Page ${item}`} value={item}>
                    {String(item).padStart(2, '0')}
                  </Pagination.Page>
                ) : (
                  <Pagination.Ellipsis>...</Pagination.Ellipsis>
                )}
              </Pagination.Item>
            ))
          }
        </Pagination.Pages>
      </Pagination.Content>
    </Pagination.Root>
  )
}

A `tabIndex` given to the group, or carried by the element `asChild` slots it onto, is left alone, and the group takes the tab stop back once that `tabIndex` is dropped. ## Data attributes | Part | Attribute | Values | | --- | --- | --- | | Root | `data-slot` | `roving-focus-group` | | Root | `data-orientation` | `horizontal`, `vertical` | | Root | `dir` | `ltr`, `rtl` | | Item | `data-slot` | `roving-focus-item` | | Item | `data-orientation` | `horizontal`, `vertical` | ## Hooks `useRovingFocusGroup(options, ref)` and `useRovingFocusItem(props, ref, enabled?)` are the group and an item without an element of their own, for a part that renders its own element, as the radio group and the menus do. ```tsx const group = useRovingFocusGroup({ orientation: 'horizontal', dir: 'ltr', loop: true }, forwardedRef) return (
) const item = useRovingFocusItem({ tabStopId: 'bold', onKeyDown }, forwardedRef) return

Unmounted 300ms after it closes, long enough for its fade.
) } ``` ### Waiting for a transition ```tsx 'use client' import { MountMinimal } from '@gentleduck/primitives/mount' import * as React from 'react' import styles from '../primitives.module.css' export function MountMinimalExample() { const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false) const panel = React.useRef(null) return (

Unmounted once the parent's grid transition ends, however long that is.
) } ``` ### Mounted once ```tsx 'use client' import { MountMinimal } from '@gentleduck/primitives/mount' import * as React from 'react' import styles from '../primitives.module.css' function Expensive() { const [mountedAt] = React.useState(() => new Date().toLocaleTimeString()) return

Mounted at {mountedAt}. It keeps its state while hidden.

} export function MountRenderOnceExample() { const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false) return (
) } ``` *** ## `Mount` Mounts its children in the commit that sets `open`, and unmounts them `animationDuration` after `open` goes false. Opening again before then keeps them. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `open` | `boolean` | - | Whether to show children | | `animationDuration` | `number` | `400` | Delay before unmounting (ms) | ```tsx
Content
 ``` ## `MountMinimal` Waits until an element's last CSS transition ends before it unmounts its children, rather than a fixed time: each transition's `transition-duration` plus its `transition-delay`, the longest of several. Under `transition-property: none`, as `motion-reduce:transition-none` leaves it, or when the browser starts no transition, as for a height going to `auto` without `interpolate-size`, they unmount at once. The element comes from `ref`, which `MountMinimal` reads and never writes: it does not render a node of its own. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `open` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether to show children | | `forceMount` | `boolean` | `false` | Keep the children mounted while closed | | `skipWaiting` | `boolean` | `false` | Unmount immediately without waiting for transitions | | `renderOnce` | `boolean` | `false` | Keep the children mounted once they have opened | | `ref` | `React.RefObject` | - | A ref object for the element whose transitions the children wait out. Without one, or with a callback ref it cannot read, they unmount as soon as it closes | ```tsx function Panel({ open }: { open: boolean }) { const ref = React.useRef(null) return (
) } ``` }> `Presence` waits for a CSS animation on the one child it wraps. Reach for `MountMinimal` when what moves is a transition on another element, such as a parent, and for `Mount` when no style says how long the exit takes.

import * as InputOTP from '@gentleduck/primitives/input-otp'
import * as React from 'react'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

export function InputOTPBasicExample() {
  const [done, setDone] = React.useState('')

  return (
    <div className={styles.stack}>
      <InputOTP.Root aria-label="Verification code" className={styles.otp} onComplete={setDone}>
        <InputOTP.Group className={styles.otp}>
          {[0, 1, 2].map((slot) => (
            <InputOTP.Slot aria-label={`Digit ${slot + 1}`} className={styles.slot} key={slot} />
          ))}
        </InputOTP.Group>
        <InputOTP.Separator>-</InputOTP.Separator>
        <InputOTP.Group className={styles.otp}>
          {[3, 4, 5].map((slot) => (
            <InputOTP.Slot aria-label={`Digit ${slot + 1}`} className={styles.slot} key={slot} />
          ))}
        </InputOTP.Group>
      </InputOTP.Root>
      <p className={styles.note}>
        {done ? `Complete: ${done}` : 'Type or paste a code. Backspace, Delete and the arrows move as in one field.'}
      </p>
    </div>
  )
}

import * as InputOTP from '@gentleduck/primitives/input-otp'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

function Code({ label, pattern }: { label: string; pattern: RegExp }) {
  return (
    <div className={styles.stack}>
      <span className={styles.label}>{label}</span>
      <InputOTP.Root aria-label={label} className={styles.otp} pattern={pattern}>
        {[0, 1, 2, 3].map((slot) => (
          <InputOTP.Slot aria-label={`${label} ${slot + 1}`} className={styles.slot} key={slot} />
        ))}
      </InputOTP.Root>
    </div>
  )
}

export function InputOTPPatternExample() {

      <Code label="Letters only" pattern={InputOTP.REGEXP_ONLY_CHARS} />
      <Code label="Hex" pattern={/^[0-9a-fA-F]$/} />
    </div>
  )
}

import * as InputOTP from '@gentleduck/primitives/input-otp'
import * as React from 'react'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

export function InputOTPFormExample() {
  const [submitted, setSubmitted] = React.useState('')

  return (
    <form
      className={styles.stack}
      onSubmit={(event) => {
        event.preventDefault()
        setSubmitted(String(new FormData(event.currentTarget).get('code')))
      }}>
      <InputOTP.Root aria-label="Code" autoSubmit className={styles.otp} defaultValue="12" name="code">
        {[0, 1, 2, 3].map((slot) => (
          <InputOTP.Slot aria-label={`Digit ${slot + 1}`} className={styles.slot} key={slot} />
        ))}
        <InputOTP.HiddenInput />
      </InputOTP.Root>
      <div className={styles.row}>
        <button className={styles.button} type="reset">
          Reset to 12
        </button>
      </div>
      <p className={styles.note}>
        {submitted
          ? `Submitted code=${submitted}`
          : 'autoSubmit sends the form once the last slot fills, under the name "code".'}
      </p>
    </form>
  )
}

import * as InputOTP from '@gentleduck/primitives/input-otp'
import * as React from 'react'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

export function InputOTPControlledExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = React.useState('')

  return (
    <div className={styles.stack}>
      <InputOTP.Root aria-label="Code" className={styles.otp} onValueChange={setValue} value={value}>
        {[0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5].map((slot) => (
          <InputOTP.Slot aria-label={`Digit ${slot + 1}`} className={styles.slot} key={slot} />
        ))}
      </InputOTP.Root>
      <div className={styles.row}>
        <button className={styles.button} onClick={() => setValue('424242')} type="button">
          Fill from SMS
        </button>
        <button className={styles.button} onClick={() => setValue('')} type="button">
          Clear
        </button>
      </div>
      <p className={styles.note}>Value: {value || 'empty'}</p>
    </div>
  )
}

import * as InputOTP from '@gentleduck/primitives/input-otp'
import * as React from 'react'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

export function InputOTPAutoFocusExample() {
  const [shown, setShown] = React.useState(false)

  return (
    <div className={styles.stack}>
      <button className={styles.button} onClick={() => setShown((value) => !value)} type="button">
        {shown ? 'Hide the code' : 'Ask for the code'}
      </button>
      {shown ? (
        <InputOTP.Root aria-label="Code" autoFocus className={styles.otp} defaultValue="5">
          {[0, 1, 2, 3].map((slot) => (
            <InputOTP.Slot aria-label={`Digit ${slot + 1}`} className={styles.slot} key={slot} />
          ))}
        </InputOTP.Root>
      ) : null}
      <p className={styles.note}>autoFocus puts the caret in the slot typing goes to, here the second.</p>
    </div>
  )
}

Typing on in the last slot of a full code replaces its character, so the code keeps its length | | A character it refuses | Nothing changes | | `Backspace` | Removes the character in the focused slot, or the one before an empty slot, and focus lands where it was | | `Delete` | Removes the character in the focused slot, and the rest of the code moves back one | | `Tab` | Stops once in the code, at the slot typing goes to: the first empty one, or the last | | `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` | Moves focus one slot, flipped in RTL | | `Enter` | Submits the form the slots sit in. A form with a submit button is left to the browser, which presses that button | | Paste | Fills from the focused slot with the characters the `pattern` accepts, as far as the slots go | | Autofill or an on-screen keyboard | Read from the input event, so a code the browser fills into one slot spreads across all of them | A slot selects its character when it takes focus. A key held with `Ctrl`, `Meta` or `Alt` is left to the browser, and the code follows what it does to the slot, so the key that deletes a word removes the slot's character. Pressing a slot past the end of the code puts the caret in the first empty slot, where typing goes. The arrow keys still reach every slot. Resetting the form puts the root back to `defaultValue`, or empties it, and a controlled root is told through `onValueChange`. A reset another listener cancels changes nothing. A browser fills a code from a text message into the slot with focus, and the root spreads it across the slots. ```tsx import { DirectionProvider, useDirection } from '@gentleduck/primitives/direction' ``` ## What it does }> `DirectionProvider` sets `ltr` or `rtl` once for a subtree. `useDirection` resolves a component's own `dir` first, then the nearest provider, then ``. This is the single direction module used by primitives and registry-ui components. A change to `` is picked up at runtime. `RTL` reads as `rtl`, and anything else, `auto` included, as `ltr`. On the server there is no document, so `useDirection` answers `ltr` there; a provider gives the right direction on first paint. The provider renders a `div` with `data-slot="direction"`, `dir` and `display: contents`. The `dir` attribute is what makes the page's CSS follow the provider, logical properties and `[dir='rtl']` selectors included, and `display: contents` keeps the `div` out of layout, so a grid or flex parent still lays out the provider's children. Those children are ordered by the parent's direction, though, so put the provider around a row that should mirror, not inside it. A child selector across the provider, such as `.list > li`, does not match, since the `div` sits between the two. ## Usage ```tsx import { DirectionProvider } from '@gentleduck/primitives/direction' import * as Dialog from '@gentleduck/primitives/dialog' export function App() { return ( Open ) } ``` ## Examples ### One provider for every primitive ```tsx 'use client' import { DirectionProvider } from '@gentleduck/primitives/direction' import * as Slider from '@gentleduck/primitives/slider' import * as ToggleGroup from '@gentleduck/primitives/toggle-group' import * as React from 'react' import styles from '../primitives.module.css' export function DirectionProviderExample() { const [dir, setDir] = React.useState<'ltr' | 'rtl'>('rtl') return (
{['start', 'center', 'end'].map((value) => ( {value} ))}

Every primitive inside reads the provider: the slider fills from the right and the arrow keys flip.

) } ``` ### Reading it in your own component ```tsx 'use client' import { DirectionProvider, useDirection } from '@gentleduck/primitives/direction' import styles from '../primitives.module.css' function Breadcrumb({ dir }: { dir?: 'ltr' | 'rtl' }) { const direction = useDirection(dir) const separator = direction === 'rtl' ? '<' : '>' return (

Home {separator} Docs {separator} Direction ({direction})

) } export function DirectionUseDirectionExample() { return (
) } ``` ### Nested providers ```tsx 'use client' import { DirectionProvider } from '@gentleduck/primitives/direction' import * as Slider from '@gentleduck/primitives/slider' import styles from '../primitives.module.css' function Volume({ label }: { label: string }) { return (
{label}
) } export function DirectionNestedExample() { return (
) } ``` *** ## API ### `DirectionProvider` | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `dir` | `'ltr' \| 'rtl'` | - | Direction for the subtree, set on its `div` and read by `useDirection` | | `children` | `React.ReactNode` | - | Wrapped subtree | ### `useDirection` ```tsx const direction = useDirection(localDir) ``` | Param | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `localDir` | `'ltr' \| 'rtl' \| undefined` | `undefined` | Optional local override | Returns: * `localDir` when provided * the nearest provider's `dir` when there is one * `'rtl'` when `` is `rtl`, and `'ltr'` otherwise, which is also the answer on the server ### Other exports | Export | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `Provider` | `React.FC<{ dir: 'ltr' \| 'rtl'; children?: ReactNode }>` | `DirectionProvider` under Radix's name | | `DirectionContext` | `React.Context<'ltr' \| 'rtl' \| undefined>` | The context the provider fills | | `DIRECTION_DICTIONARY` | `{ ltr: 'ltr'; rtl: 'rtl' }` | The two values |

export function PopoverAnchorExample() {
  return (
    <Popover.Root>
      <Popover.Anchor className={`${styles.box} ${styles.row}`}>
        <input className={styles.input} placeholder="Search..." />
        <Popover.Trigger className={styles.button}>Filters</Popover.Trigger>
      </Popover.Anchor>
      <Popover.Portal>

      </Popover.Portal>
    </Popover.Root>
  )
}

import * as Popover from '@gentleduck/primitives/popover'
import * as React from 'react'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

export function PopoverFocusExample() {
  const comment = React.useRef<HTMLTextAreaElement>(null)

  return (
    <Popover.Root>
      <Popover.Trigger className={styles.button}>Comment</Popover.Trigger>
      <Popover.Portal>
        <Popover.Content
          className={`${styles.content} ${styles.panel} ${styles.stack}`}
          initialFocus={comment}
          sideOffset={8}>
          <button className={styles.button} type="button">
            Attach
          </button>
          <textarea className={styles.input} placeholder="Focus starts here" ref={comment} rows={3} />
        </Popover.Content>
      </Popover.Portal>
    </Popover.Root>
  )
}

import * as Popover from '@gentleduck/primitives/popover'
import * as React from 'react'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

export function PopoverControlledExample() {
  const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false)
  const [color, setColor] = React.useState('blue')

  return (
    <Popover.Root onOpenChange={setOpen} open={open}>
      <Popover.Trigger className={styles.button}>Color: {color}</Popover.Trigger>
      <Popover.Portal>
        <Popover.Content className={`${styles.content} ${styles.panel} ${styles.row}`} sideOffset={8}>
          {['blue', 'green', 'orange'].map((value) => (
            <button
              className={styles.button}
              key={value}
              onClick={() => {
                setColor(value)
                setOpen(false)
              }}
              type="button">
              {value}
            </button>
          ))}
        </Popover.Content>
      </Popover.Portal>
    </Popover.Root>
  )
}

import * as Slider from '@gentleduck/primitives/slider'
import * as React from 'react'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

export function SliderRangeExample() {
  const [range, setRange] = React.useState([200, 800])

  return (
    <div className={styles.stack}>
      <Slider.Root
        className={styles.slider}
        max={1000}
        minStepsBetweenThumbs={10}
        onValueChange={setRange}
        preserveThumbOrder
        step={10}
        value={range}>
        <Slider.Track className={styles.track}>
          <Slider.Range className={styles.range} />
        </Slider.Track>
        <Slider.Thumb aria-label="Minimum price" className={styles.thumb} />
        <Slider.Thumb aria-label="Maximum price" className={styles.thumb} />
      </Slider.Root>
      <p className={styles.note}>
        ${range[0]} to ${range[1]}. The thumbs stop 10 steps apart instead of crossing.
      </p>
    </div>
  )
}

import * as Slider from '@gentleduck/primitives/slider'
import * as React from 'react'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

export function SliderCommitExample() {
  const [live, setLive] = React.useState([30])
  const [saved, setSaved] = React.useState([30])

  return (
    <div className={styles.stack}>
      <Slider.Root className={styles.slider} onValueChange={setLive} onValueCommit={setSaved} value={live}>
        <Slider.Track className={styles.track}>
          <Slider.Range className={styles.range} />
        </Slider.Track>
        <Slider.Thumb aria-label="Brightness" className={styles.thumb} />
      </Slider.Root>
      <p className={styles.note}>
        While dragging: {live[0]}. Saved once the drag ends: {saved[0]}.
      </p>
    </div>
  )
}

import * as Slider from '@gentleduck/primitives/slider'
import * as React from 'react'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

export function SliderFormExample() {
  const [sent, setSent] = React.useState('')

  return (
    <form
      className={styles.stack}
      onSubmit={(event) => {
        event.preventDefault()
        setSent(new FormData(event.currentTarget).getAll('budget').join(' to '))
      }}>
      <Slider.Root className={styles.slider} defaultValue={[20, 60]} name="budget">

          <Slider.Range className={styles.range} />

          Search
        </button>
        <button className={styles.button} type="reset">
          Reset
        </button>
      </div>
      <p className={styles.note}>
        {sent ? `Submitted budget=${sent}` : 'Each thumb submits a value under the name budget.'}
      </p>
    </form>
  )
}

Renders a ``. Inside a form, or with `form`, each thumb renders a hidden ``, so the values submit under `name` (as `name[]` with more than one thumb), and a form reset restores the values the slider started with, in an iframe too, and leaves focus where it is. A press with the main button moves the closest thumb to the pointer and focuses it, even when the value stays where it was. A press on a thumb, or on anything inside it, focuses that thumb without moving it. A right click or a Control click moves nothing, since each opens the context menu. A drag the browser cancels ends where it stopped, as a pointer up does. A change the user makes dispatches a bubbling `input` event from that hidden input, so a form's `onChange` and an ancestor's `onInput` both hear it, including a value a controlled parent adjusts in the same render. Resolved with `useDirection` (`dir` prop -> `DirectionProvider` -> ``), and written on the root alone, which the parts inherit. | | `min` | `number` | `0` | Minimum allowed value | | `max` | `number` | `100` | Maximum allowed value | | `step` | `number` | `1` | Increment step for values | | `value` | `number[]` | - | Controlled values array | | `defaultValue` | `number[]` | `[min]` | Uncontrolled initial values | | `onValueChange` | `(value: number[]) => void` | - | Called on every value change during interaction | | `onValueCommit` | `(value: number[]) => void` | - | Called once when the user finishes an interaction that changed any value (pointer up, a cancelled drag, or a key) | | `inverted` | `boolean` | `false` | Inverts the slider direction | | `largeStep` | `number` | ten steps | How far PageUp, PageDown and Shift with an arrow key move a thumb, as in Base UI. Give a multiple of `step` | | `minStepsBetweenThumbs` | `number` | `0` | Minimum number of steps required between thumbs | | `preserveThumbOrder` | `boolean` | `false` | Stops a thumb at its neighbour, `minStepsBetweenThumbs` away from it, instead of letting it cross and swap places | | `form` | `string` | - | Associates hidden inputs with a form element by ID | Exposes `data-disabled` and `data-orientation` attributes. Sets the CSS custom property `--gentleduck-slider-thumb-transform` for thumb positioning. ### `Slider.Track` The track area the thumbs slide along. Renders a ``. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `asChild` | `boolean` | - | Render as child element | Exposes `data-disabled` and `data-orientation` attributes. ### `Slider.Range` The filled portion between thumbs (or from min to a single thumb). Renders a ``. Positioned automatically via inline styles. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `asChild` | `boolean` | - | Render as child element | Exposes `data-disabled` and `data-orientation` attributes. ### `Slider.Thumb` A draggable thumb. Once it mounts, its index comes from its render order. On the server that order is not known yet, so a lone thumb renders at the slider's one value, and each thumb of a range renders hidden unless given `index`. Renders a `` with `role="slider"`, and inside a form a hidden `` for submission. After a change, focus moves to the thumb that changed, showing the focus ring only when a key moved it. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `name` | `string` | - | Optional name override for this thumb's hidden input | | `index` | `number` | - | Where the thumb sits among the values until it mounts, so a range renders its thumbs on the server | | `asChild` | `boolean` | - | Render as child element | Sets `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemax`, and `aria-orientation` automatically, and `aria-disabled` when the slider is disabled. Exposes `data-disabled` and `data-orientation` attributes. ### `Slider.Value` The values as text, as Base UI's `Slider.Value`, Ark's `ValueText` and React Aria's `SliderOutput` show them, following each thumb as it moves. Renders a `` hidden from assistive technology, since each thumb already announces its own value. Without children it shows the values joined with a comma. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `children` | `ReactNode \| ((values: number[]) => ReactNode)` | - | What to show in place of the values, or a function of them | ```tsx {([low, high]) => `$${low} to $${high}`} ``` Exposes `data-disabled` and `data-orientation` attributes. ### `Slider.ThumbProvider` / `Slider.ThumbTrigger` / `Slider.BubbleInput` `Slider.Thumb` is `Slider.ThumbTrigger` inside a `Slider.ThumbProvider`, with a `Slider.BubbleInput` beside it when the slider is in a form. Compose the three yourself to place the hidden input, give it props of its own, or render it outside a form. ```tsx ``` `Slider.ThumbProvider` takes the thumb's `name` and `index`. `Slider.ThumbTrigger` takes the props of `Slider.Thumb` except `name`. `Slider.BubbleInput` takes the props of an `` except `value`, which comes from the thumb. *** ## Keyboard interactions | Key | Action | | --- | --- | | ArrowRight | Increments by one step (horizontal LTR) | | ArrowLeft | Decrements by one step (horizontal LTR) | | ArrowUp | Increments by one step (vertical) | | ArrowDown | Decrements by one step (vertical) | | PageUp | Increments by `largeStep`, ten steps by default | | PageDown | Decrements by `largeStep`, ten steps by default | | Shift + ArrowKey | Increments/decrements by `largeStep` | | Home | Sets the focused thumb to the minimum value | | End | Sets the focused thumb to the maximum value | A value off the `step` grid, such as one set through `value`, moves to the next grid line in the direction of the key first, and that counts as one of the steps.

Renders a ``. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `asChild` | `boolean` | - | Render as child element | Exposes `data-disabled` and `data-orientation` attributes. ### `Slider.Range` The filled portion between thumbs (or from min to a single thumb). Renders a ``. Positioned automatically via inline styles. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `asChild` | `boolean` | - | Render as child element | Exposes `data-disabled` and `data-orientation` attributes. ### `Slider.Thumb` A draggable thumb. Once it mounts, its index comes from its render order. On the server that order is not known yet, so a lone thumb renders at the slider's one value, and each thumb of a range renders hidden unless given `index`. Renders a `` with `role="slider"`, and inside a form a hidden `` for submission. Without children it shows the values joined with a comma. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `children` | `ReactNode \| ((values: number[]) => ReactNode)` | - | What to show in place of the values, or a function of them | ```tsx {([low, high]) => `$${low} to $${high}`} ``` Exposes `data-disabled` and `data-orientation` attributes. ### `Slider.ThumbProvider` / `Slider.ThumbTrigger` / `Slider.BubbleInput` `Slider.Thumb` is `Slider.ThumbTrigger` inside a `Slider.ThumbProvider`, with a `Slider.BubbleInput` beside it when the slider is in a form. Opens on right-click on the trigger area. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `open` | `boolean` | - | Controlled open state. Close the menu by setting it to `false` | | `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` | - | Called when open state changes | | `dir` | `'ltr' \| 'rtl'` | - | Reading direction of the menu. The trigger keeps the page's | | `modal` | `boolean` | `true` | Enable modal behavior | A context menu opens where the pointer is, so setting `open` to `true` before the trigger is right-clicked opens it at the top-left corner of the viewport, and warns once in development. Open it from `onOpenChange` and use `open` to close it or keep it closed. ### `ContextMenu.Trigger` The area that responds to right-click. Renders a `` by default. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Ignore right-clicks and long presses, so the browser's own menu shows | A touch or pen press held for 700ms opens the menu too, unless it moves more than 10px first or a second finger comes down, so a pinch opens nothing. A long press while the menu is open closes it and any submenu, then opens it again where you pressed. With triggers nested inside each other, only the innermost one opens. A right-click or control-click while the menu is open closes it rather than opening it again where the pointer is. A menu still mounted while closed, by `forceMount`, opens where the new right click lands. ### `ContextMenu.Portal` Renders the content into a portal. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `container` | `Element \| DocumentFragment \| RefObject \| null` | `document.body` | Portal target | | `forceMount` | `true` | - | Keep the content mounted while closed. A submenu takes it only from its own prop or a portal of its own | ### `ContextMenu.Content` The menu content. Positioned at the cursor location. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `forceMount` | `true` | - | Keep mounted regardless of open state | | `trapFocus` | `boolean` | `open` | Modal only. Override whether focus is trapped inside the content | | `disableOutsidePointerEvents` | `boolean` | `open` | Modal only. Override whether pointer events outside are blocked | | `disableOutsideScroll` | `boolean` | `true` | Modal only. Override whether body scroll is locked while open | | `loop` | `boolean` | `false` | Arrow keys wrap from the last item to the first and back | | `onPointerDownOutside` | `(event) => void` | - | Called when clicking outside | | `onFocusOutside` | `(event) => void` | - | Called when focus moves outside | | `onInteractOutside` | `(event) => void` | - | Called for any outside interaction | | `onEscapeKeyDown` | `(event) => void` | - | Called when Escape is pressed | | `onCloseAutoFocus` | `(event: Event) => void` | - | Called when focus returns on close | On a modal menu, `trapFocus` and `disableOutsidePointerEvents` follow the open state and `disableOutsideScroll` is on. Override them when integrating with animation libraries like [motion](https://motion.dev) that need custom lifecycle control during exit animations. A non-modal menu never traps focus, blocks outside pointer events or locks scroll, and ignores all three. It opens at the pointer, so it takes no `side`, `sideOffset` or `align`, and takes the rest of [Popper](/duck-primitives/api/popper)'s positioning props with the same defaults: `alignOffset`, `arrowPadding`, `avoidCollisions`, `collisionBoundary`, `collisionPadding`, `sticky`, `shiftCrossAxis`, `hideWhenDetached`, `updatePositionStrategy` and `updateOnScroll`. The menu closes, with any open submenu, when the window loses focus. Kept mounted with `forceMount`, it takes focus each time it opens rather than when it mounts closed, and a modal one leaves the page to screen readers while it is closed. A menu that is closing but still mounted lets no item take focus under the pointer. ### `ContextMenu.Item` A menu item. Fires `onSelect` when activated. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disable the item | | `onSelect` | `(event) => void` | - | Called when item is selected | | `closeOnSelect` | `boolean` | `true` | Close the menu once the item is selected. A checkbox or radio item takes it too | | `textValue` | `string` | - | Text typeahead matches, in place of the text the item shows | Exposes `data-highlighted` when focused and `data-disabled` when disabled. A key typed into a focusable element inside the item, even one portalled out of it, is left to that element. A disabled item rendered as a link with `asChild` does not follow the link. ### `ContextMenu.CheckboxItem` A toggleable menu item with checked state. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `checked` | `boolean \| 'indeterminate'` | - | Checked state | | `onCheckedChange` | `(checked: boolean) => void` | - | Called on toggle | It takes `disabled`, `onSelect`, `closeOnSelect` and `textValue` as `ContextMenu.Item` does. ### `ContextMenu.RadioGroup` / `ContextMenu.RadioItem` Mutually exclusive menu items. | Prop (RadioGroup) | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `value` | `string` | - | The checked item's value | | `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | - | Called with the value of the item chosen | | Prop (RadioItem) | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `value` | `string` | - | Value for this item | A radio item takes `disabled`, `onSelect`, `closeOnSelect` and `textValue` as `ContextMenu.Item` does. ### `ContextMenu.Sub` / `ContextMenu.SubTrigger` / `ContextMenu.SubContent` Nested submenus. The sub-trigger points `aria-controls` at its submenu only while the submenu is open, since the id names nothing while it is closed. `ContextMenu.Sub` takes `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` and `closeParentOnEsc`, as `DropdownMenu.Sub` does. With `closeParentOnEsc={false}`, Escape inside the submenu closes only the submenu and focuses its sub-trigger. `ContextMenu.SubTrigger` takes `disabled` and `textValue`. `ContextMenu.SubContent` takes `forceMount`, `loop`, the outside handlers and Popper's positioning props, `sideOffset` and `alignOffset` included. A submenu flipped to the left stays open when the pointer moves straight into it in one jump. ### `ContextMenu.Separator` Visual separator between groups. ### `ContextMenu.Label` Non-interactive label for a group. *** ## Keyboard interactions | Key | Action | | --- | --- | | ArrowDown | Highlight next item | | ArrowUp | Highlight previous item | | A letter | Highlight the next item whose text starts with it, read from the label each item shows now. Typing the focused item's name keeps focus on it, and a letter typed into a field inside the menu is left to the field | | ArrowRight | Open submenu (on SubTrigger) | | ArrowLeft | Close submenu | | Enter / Space | Activate highlighted item | | Escape | Close the menu, or only a submenu given `closeParentOnEsc={false}` |

A press that waits and gets no click, such as a touch that turns into a scroll, is let go when the mouse lifts or the touch is cancelled, so focus leaving the layer dismisses it again and a later click does not. The press that opened the layer reaches the document after the layer mounts and does not dismiss it. Any press made after the mount does, even one the browser runs before its timers on a busy page. A press on a scrollbar outside the layer scrolls without dismissing it, whether the scrollbar belongs to a box on the page or to the page itself, and so does the focus that press gives a focusable box. So does a press on a scrollbar macOS draws over the edge of a box or the page, taking no room. Nothing on the event tells it from a press on the content under it, so a primary press within 17 pixels of that edge waits for its click, which only a press on the content sends, and `onPointerDownOutside` is called once that click lands. Inside a shadow root the layer reads each event's target from its composed path and also listens for focus on the shadow root, since focus moving between two of its elements never reaches the document. It leaves a layer in this document its pointer events and its presses outside. A press inside the layer that a handler stops before it reaches the document, or whose `onPointerDownCapture` prevents the default, still counts as inside, so the next press outside dismisses the layer as it should. The layer works from its element. With `asChild`, a child that never takes the ref leaves the layer out of the stack, so nothing dismisses it. Content that attaches it later, such as through a child's `asChild`, uses `DismissableLayer`. ## useDismissableLayerSurface Returns a ref callback for a node, such as a dialog's overlay, that dismisses the layer even when its own handlers stop propagation. Like branches, surfaces count for every layer on the page: ```tsx const ref = useDismissableLayerSurface() return
``` ## DismissableLayerBranch }> Marks a DOM subtree as "part of" the dismissable layer. Clicks inside a branch won't trigger dismissal. Useful for toasts or notifications that relate to the overlay but render outside it. }> Used internally by the content of Dialog, Popover, Tooltip, Hover Card, Select, Navigation Menu and every menu. Dialog and Popover defer their outside press, and `Dialog.Overlay` is a surface.

))} ) } ``` *** ## API ### `Popper.Root` Connects an anchor to its content. It renders nothing of its own. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `anchor` | `IPopper.IMeasurable \| null` | - | The element to place the content against, for a component that already holds it, in place of a `Popper.Anchor` | ### `Popper.Anchor` The reference element that content is positioned relative to. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `virtualRef` | `React.RefObject` | - | Position relative to a virtual element instead of a DOM node: anything with `getBoundingClientRect()`. The anchor then renders nothing | While the content is mounted, the anchor element carries `data-popper-side` and `data-popper-align`: where the content was placed, after any flip. The trigger of a Popover, Select, Tooltip, Hover Card or menu is its anchor, so it can point a chevron at its content with `data-[popper-side=top]:rotate-180`. A virtual anchor gets neither. The content itself carries `data-side` and `data-align`. ### `Popper.Content` The floating content. Positioned relative to the anchor, inside a wrapper with `data-slot="popper-content-wrapper"` that is `position: fixed` and takes the content's `z-index`. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `side` | `'top' \| 'right' \| 'bottom' \| 'left'` | `'bottom'` | Preferred side relative to anchor | | `sideOffset` | `number` | `0` | Gap between content and anchor (px) | | `align` | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end'` | `'center'` | Alignment along the side | | `alignOffset` | `number` | `0` | Alignment offset (px) | | `arrowPadding` | `number` | `0` | Space kept between the arrow and the content's edges (px). Against an anchor too small for it, the content slides over so the arrow still points at the anchor's middle | | `avoidCollisions` | `boolean` | `true` | Flip and shift to stay inside the boundary | | `collisionBoundary` | `Element \| null \| Array` | `[]` | Elements to stay inside, besides the viewport. A `null` is skipped | | `collisionPadding` | `number \| Partial>` | `0` | Space kept from the boundary's edges (px), on every side or per side | | `sticky` | `'partial' \| 'always'` | `'partial'` | `'partial'` stops shifting once the content would leave its anchor; `'always'` keeps it in the boundary regardless | | `shiftCrossAxis` | `boolean` | `false` | Also shift along the side's own axis, such as vertically for a top or bottom placement | | `hideWhenDetached` | `boolean` | `false` | Hide content once the anchor is out of view: scrolled out of a scrolling box or the viewport, or out of `collisionBoundary` when set | | `updatePositionStrategy` | `'optimized' \| 'always'` | `'optimized'` | `'optimized'` measures again on scroll, resize and layout changes; `'always'` on every animation frame, for an anchor that moves by itself | | `updateOnScroll` | `boolean` | `true` | Measure again when a box around the anchor scrolls. Off for content that closes when its anchor scrolls, such as a tooltip, which has no scroll to follow | | `onPlaced` | `() => void` | - | Called once the content has been positioned | `side="left"` and `side="right"` mirror in right to left. The direction comes from `dir` on the content, then the nearest `DirectionProvider`, then ``, and the wrapper carries the provider's, so content portalled out of a `DirectionProvider` still aligns its `start` the way the provider reads. Until the content is positioned, the wrapper sits off screen and the content's `animation` is `none`, so an entry animation starts from where it opens. An `animation` in its `style` runs once it is placed. The wrapper sets these variables for the content to read: | Variable | Value | | --- | --- | | `--gentleduck-popper-transform-origin` | The point the content grows from: the arrow's tip, or the anchor's edge when there is no arrow | | `--gentleduck-popper-available-width` | Room left inside the boundary along the width | | `--gentleduck-popper-available-height` | Room left inside the boundary along the height | | `--gentleduck-popper-anchor-width` | The anchor's width | | `--gentleduck-popper-anchor-height` | The anchor's height | ### `Popper.Arrow` An SVG arrow pointing at the anchor, on the side of the content facing it. It hides when it cannot point at the anchor's center without leaving the content. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `width` | `number` | `10` | Width (px) | | `height` | `number` | `5` | Height (px), added to `sideOffset` | | `asChild` | `boolean` | `false` | Draw your own SVG children instead of the default path | ## How it works }> Popper measures the anchor element's rect, calculates the content position based on `side` and `align`, and adjusts if the content would overflow the viewport (when `avoidCollisions` is true). }> You rarely use Popper directly. Popover, Tooltip, Hover Card, and Menu use it internally for positioning.

function ToppingsSelect() {
  const [toppings, setToppings] = React.useState<string[]>([])

  return (
    <Select.Root multiple name="toppings" onValueChange={setToppings} value={toppings}>
      <Select.Trigger aria-label="Toppings" className="px-3 py-2 border rounded">
        <Select.Value placeholder="Pick toppings" />
        <Select.Icon />
      </Select.Trigger>

          <Select.Viewport className="p-1">

                <Select.ItemText>{topping}</Select.ItemText>
                <Select.ItemIndicator>*</Select.ItemIndicator>
              </Select.Item>
            ))}
          </Select.Viewport>
        </Select.Content>
      </Select.Portal>
    </Select.Root>

import * as Select from '@gentleduck/primitives/select'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

export function SelectBasicExample() {
  return (
    <Select.Root defaultValue="banana">
      <Select.Trigger aria-label="Fruit" className={styles.trigger}>
        <Select.Value placeholder="Pick a fruit" />
        <Select.Icon>v</Select.Icon>
      </Select.Trigger>
      <Select.Portal>
        <Select.Content className={styles.content}>
          <Select.ScrollUpButton className={styles.note}>^</Select.ScrollUpButton>
          <Select.Viewport>
            <Select.Group>
              <Select.Label className={styles.groupLabel}>Fruit</Select.Label>
              {['Apple', 'Banana', 'Cherry'].map((fruit) => (
                <Select.Item className={styles.item} key={fruit} value={fruit.toLowerCase()}>
                  <Select.ItemText>{fruit}</Select.ItemText>
                  <Select.ItemIndicator className={styles.shortcut}>x</Select.ItemIndicator>
                </Select.Item>
              ))}
            </Select.Group>
            <Select.Separator className={styles.separator} />
            <Select.Group>
              <Select.Label className={styles.groupLabel}>Vegetables</Select.Label>
              <Select.Item className={styles.item} value="carrot">
                <Select.ItemText>Carrot</Select.ItemText>
              </Select.Item>
              <Select.Item className={styles.item} disabled value="leek">
                <Select.ItemText>Leek (out of season)</Select.ItemText>
              </Select.Item>
            </Select.Group>
          </Select.Viewport>
          <Select.ScrollDownButton className={styles.note}>v</Select.ScrollDownButton>
        </Select.Content>
      </Select.Portal>
    </Select.Root>
  )
}

import * as React from 'react'
import styles from './styles.module.css'

export function SelectControlledInternalExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = React.useState('apple')

  return (
    <Select.Select value={value} onValueChange={setValue}>
      <Select.SelectTrigger className={styles.trigger}>
        <Select.SelectValue placeholder="Choose fruit" />
      </Select.SelectTrigger>
      <Select.SelectPortal>
        <Select.SelectContent className={styles.content} sideOffset={8}>

            </Select.SelectItem>
          </Select.SelectViewport>
        </Select.SelectContent>
      </Select.SelectPortal>
    </Select.Select>
  )
}

import * as Select from '@gentleduck/primitives/select'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

export function SelectPopperExample() {
  return (
    <Select.Root defaultValue="utc">
      <Select.Trigger aria-label="Time zone" className={styles.trigger}>
        <Select.Value />
      </Select.Trigger>
      <Select.Portal>
        <Select.Content
          className={styles.content}
          position="popper"
          sideOffset={6}
          style={{ minWidth: 'var(--gentleduck-select-trigger-width)' }}>
          <Select.Viewport>
            {['utc', 'cet', 'est', 'pst'].map((zone) => (
              <Select.Item className={styles.item} key={zone} value={zone}>
                <Select.ItemText>{zone.toUpperCase()}</Select.ItemText>
              </Select.Item>
            ))}
          </Select.Viewport>
          <Select.Arrow className={styles.arrow} />
        </Select.Content>
      </Select.Portal>
    </Select.Root>

import * as Select from '@gentleduck/primitives/select'
import * as React from 'react'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

const TAGS = ['design', 'frontend', 'backend', 'docs', 'testing']

export function SelectMultipleExample() {
  const [tags, setTags] = React.useState<string[]>(['frontend'])

  return (
    <Select.Root multiple onValueChange={setTags} value={tags}>
      <Select.Trigger aria-label="Tags" className={styles.trigger}>
        <Select.Value placeholder="No tags">{(picked) => `${picked.length} tags: ${picked.join(', ')}`}</Select.Value>
      </Select.Trigger>
      <Select.Portal>
        <Select.Content className={styles.content} position="popper" sideOffset={6}>
          <Select.Viewport>
            {TAGS.map((tag) => (
              <Select.Item className={styles.item} key={tag} value={tag}>
                <Select.ItemIndicator>x</Select.ItemIndicator>
                <Select.ItemText>{tag}</Select.ItemText>
              </Select.Item>
            ))}
          </Select.Viewport>
        </Select.Content>
      </Select.Portal>
    </Select.Root>

import * as Select from '@gentleduck/primitives/select'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

const COUNTRIES = [
  { value: 'de', label: 'Germany' },
  { value: 'eg', label: 'Egypt' },
  { value: 'jp', label: 'Japan' },
  { value: 'kp', label: 'North Korea', disabled: true },
]

export function SelectItemsExample() {
  return (
    <Select.Root defaultValue="eg" items={COUNTRIES}>
      <Select.Trigger aria-label="Country" className={styles.trigger}>
        <Select.Value />
      </Select.Trigger>
      <Select.Portal>
        <Select.Content className={styles.content}>
          <Select.Viewport>
            {COUNTRIES.map((country) => (
              <Select.Item
                className={styles.item}
                disabled={country.disabled}
                key={country.value}
                value={country.value}>
                <Select.ItemText>{country.label}</Select.ItemText>
              </Select.Item>
            ))}
          </Select.Viewport>
        </Select.Content>
      </Select.Portal>
    </Select.Root>
  )
}

import * as Select from '@gentleduck/primitives/select'
import * as React from 'react'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

export function SelectFormExample() {
  const [sent, setSent] = React.useState('')

  return (
    <form
      className={styles.stack}
      onSubmit={(event) => {
        event.preventDefault()
        setSent(String(new FormData(event.currentTarget).get('role')))
      }}>
      <Select.Root autoComplete="organization-title" name="role" required>
        <Select.Trigger aria-label="Role" className={styles.trigger}>
          <Select.Value placeholder="Pick a role" />
        </Select.Trigger>
        <Select.Portal>
          <Select.Content className={styles.content}>
            <Select.Viewport>
              {['viewer', 'editor', 'owner'].map((role) => (
                <Select.Item className={styles.item} key={role} value={role}>
                  <Select.ItemText>{role}</Select.ItemText>
                </Select.Item>
              ))}
            </Select.Viewport>
          </Select.Content>
        </Select.Portal>
      </Select.Root>
      <div className={styles.row}>
        <button className={`${styles.button} ${styles.primary}`} type="submit">
          Invite
        </button>
        <button className={styles.button} type="reset">
          Reset
        </button>
      </div>
      <p className={styles.note}>
        {sent ? `Submitted role=${sent}` : 'name submits the pick, required refuses an empty one.'}
      </p>
    </form>
  )
}

import * as Select from '@gentleduck/primitives/select'
import * as React from 'react'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

export function SelectControlledOpenExample() {
  const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false)

  return (
    <div className={styles.row}>
      <Select.Root onOpenChange={setOpen} open={open}>
        <Select.Trigger aria-label="Priority" className={styles.trigger}>
          <Select.Value placeholder="Priority" />
        </Select.Trigger>
        <Select.Portal>
          <Select.Content className={styles.content} position="popper" sideOffset={6}>
            <Select.Viewport>
              {['low', 'medium', 'high'].map((level) => (
                <Select.Item className={styles.item} key={level} value={level}>
                  <Select.ItemText>{level}</Select.ItemText>
                </Select.Item>
              ))}
            </Select.Viewport>
          </Select.Content>
        </Select.Portal>
      </Select.Root>
      <button className={styles.button} onClick={() => setOpen(true)} type="button">
        Open from here
      </button>
    </div>
  )
}

import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

export function SelectRtlExample() {
  return (

      <Select.Portal>
        <Select.Content className={styles.content}>
          <Select.Viewport>

              </Select.Item>

        </Select.Content>
      </Select.Portal>
    </Select.Root>
  )
}
