```tsx import * as Select from '@gentleduck/primitives/select' ``` ## Anatomy ```tsx ``` *** ## Usage ```tsx import * as Select from '@gentleduck/primitives/select' function ThemeSelect() { return ( Light * Dark * System * ) } ``` ## Multiple With `multiple`, the select holds a list of values. `value`, `defaultValue` and `onValueChange` take and give `string[]` in the order the values were picked, and TypeScript reads which from the prop. ```tsx import * as Select from '@gentleduck/primitives/select' import * as React from 'react' function ToppingsSelect() { const [toppings, setToppings] = React.useState([]) return ( {['Basil', 'Mushroom', 'Olive'].map((topping) => ( {topping} * ))} ) } ``` * A click, Enter or Space toggles the item and leaves the list open. Escape or a press outside closes it. * `Select.Value` shows the picked labels joined by ", ", or the placeholder while none is picked. A function given as its child is called with the picked values instead. * The listbox carries `aria-multiselectable`, and every option says with `aria-selected` whether it is picked. * The hidden native select is a ``, so the value submits under `name`, autofill can set it, and a form reset restores the value the select started with. The reset is heard once it has bubbled, from the form the select belongs to at that moment, so a form named by `form` that mounts later still resets it and a reset a handler cancels leaves it alone. When the browser changes the native select, as autofill does, and a controlled owner does not take the change, the native select goes back to the owner's value. A pick by the user dispatches a bubbling `change` event from that native select, so a form's `onChange` hears it, unless the item's handler stopped propagation. A change made through `value` updates the native select without bubbling. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `multiple` | `boolean` | `false` | Holds a list of values. See [Multiple](#multiple). | | `value` | `string \| string[]` | - | Controlled selected value, a list in pick order with `multiple` | | `defaultValue` | `string \| string[]` | - | Initial value (uncontrolled), a list with `multiple` | | `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | - | Called when the selected value changes. With `multiple` it is given `string[]`. | | `open` | `boolean` | - | Controlled open state | | `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Initial open state (uncontrolled) | | `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` | - | Called when the open state should change | | `dir` | `'ltr' \| 'rtl'` | - | Text direction. Resolved with `useDirection` (`dir` prop -> `DirectionProvider` -> ``). | | `name` | `string` | - | Name for native form submission | | `autoComplete` | `string` | - | Hint for browser autofill | | `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Disables the select | | `required` | `boolean` | - | Marks as required for form validation. With `multiple`, one pick satisfies it. | | `form` | `string` | - | Associates with a form element by ID | | `items` | `{ value: string; label: string; disabled?: boolean }[]` | - | The items, as data. A closed select then renders none of its items: the trigger's label, the native `` still lists each item once | | `side` | `'top' \| 'right' \| 'bottom' \| 'left'` | `'bottom'` | Preferred side (popper only) | | `sideOffset` | `number` | - | Main-axis offset (popper only) | | `align` | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end'` | `'start'` | Cross-axis alignment (popper only) | | `alignOffset` | `number` | - | Cross-axis offset (popper only) | | `avoidCollisions` | `boolean` | `true` | Flip to avoid viewport overflow (popper only) | | `collisionBoundary` | `Element \| Element[]` | - | Custom collision boundary (popper only) | | `collisionPadding` | `number` | `10` | Padding from viewport edges | | `arrowPadding` | `number` | `0` | Minimum padding between arrow and content edges (popper only) | | `sticky` | `'partial' \| 'always'` | `'partial'` | Keep content in view when trigger is partially hidden (popper only) | | `hideWhenDetached` | `boolean` | `false` | Hide content once the trigger is scrolled out of view (popper only) | | `shiftCrossAxis` | `boolean` | `false` | Also shift along the side's own axis (popper only) | | `updatePositionStrategy` | `'optimized' \| 'always'` | `'optimized'` | Measure on scroll, resize and layout changes, or on every frame (popper only) | | `updateOnScroll` | `boolean` | `true` | Measure again when a box around the trigger scrolls (popper only) | | `onCloseAutoFocus` | `(event: Event) => void` | - | Called when focus returns to trigger on close | | `onEscapeKeyDown` | `(event: KeyboardEvent) => void` | - | Called when Escape is pressed | | `onPointerDownOutside` | `(event) => void` | - | Called when clicking outside | | `onFocusOutside` | `(event) => void` | - | Called when focus moves outside. import * as Command from '@gentleduck/primitives/command'
import * as React from 'react'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

export function CommandPaletteExample() {
  const [last, setLast] = React.useState('nothing yet')

  return (
    <div className={styles.stack}>
      <Command.Root className={styles.command} aria-label="Command palette">
        <Command.Input className={styles.commandInput} placeholder="Type a command or search..." />
        <Command.List className={styles.commandList}>
          <Command.Empty className={styles.commandEmpty}>No results.</Command.Empty>
          <Command.Group heading="Suggestions">
            <Command.Item className={styles.item} keywords={['agenda', 'schedule']} onSelect={setLast} value="calendar">
              Calendar
            </Command.Item>
            <Command.Item className={styles.item} keywords={['emoji']} onSelect={setLast} value="smileys">
              Search emoji
            </Command.Item>
          </Command.Group>
          <Command.Separator className={styles.separator} />
          <Command.Group heading="Settings">
            <Command.Item className={styles.item} onSelect={setLast} value="profile">
              Profile <span className={styles.shortcut}>Ctrl P</span>
            </Command.Item>
            <Command.Item className={styles.item} onSelect={setLast} value="billing">
              Billing <span className={styles.shortcut}>Ctrl B</span>
            </Command.Item>
          </Command.Group>
        </Command.List>
      </Command.Root>
      <p className={styles.note}>Selected: {last}. "agenda" finds Calendar through its keywords.</p>
    </div>
  )
}

import * as Command from '@gentleduck/primitives/command'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

const COUNTRIES = [
  'Austria',
  'Australia',
  'Belgium',
  'Brazil',
  'Canada',
  'Chile',
  'China',
  'Denmark',
  'Egypt',
  'Estonia',
]

// A start of the name ranks first, a match elsewhere in it second.
function prefixFirst(text: string, search: string) {
  const name = text.toLowerCase()
  const query = search.toLowerCase()
  if (name.startsWith(query)) return 1
  return name.includes(query) ? 0.5 : 0
}

export function CommandFilterExample() {
  return (
    <Command.Root className={styles.command} filter={prefixFirst} aria-label="Countries" limit={4}>
      <Command.Input className={styles.commandInput} placeholder="Search countries..." />
      <Command.List className={styles.commandList}>
        <Command.Empty className={styles.commandEmpty}>No country matches.</Command.Empty>
        {COUNTRIES.map((country) => (
          <Command.Item className={styles.item} key={country} value={country}>
            {country}
          </Command.Item>
        ))}
      </Command.List>
    </Command.Root>
  )
}

import * as Command from '@gentleduck/primitives/command'
import * as React from 'react'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

const PACKAGES = ['react', 'react-dom', 'react-router', 'redux', 'remix', 'rollup', 'rxjs', 'vite', 'vitest', 'vue']

function Results({ onLoading }: { onLoading: (loading: boolean) => void }) {
  const search = Command.useCommandSearch()
  const [hits, setHits] = React.useState<string[]>([])

  React.useEffect(() => {
    onLoading(true)
    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
      setHits(search ? PACKAGES.filter((name) => name.includes(search.toLowerCase())) : [])
      onLoading(false)
    }, 400)
    return () => clearTimeout(timer)
  }, [search, onLoading])

  return hits.map((name) => (
    <Command.Item className={styles.item} key={name} value={name}>
      {name}
    </Command.Item>
  ))
}

export function CommandAsyncExample() {
  const [loading, setLoading] = React.useState(false)

  return (
    <Command.Root className={styles.command} aria-label="Packages" shouldFilter={false}>
      <Command.Input className={styles.commandInput} placeholder="Search packages..." />
      <Command.Status className={styles.note} style={{ padding: '0.3rem 0.75rem' }}>
        {(count) => (loading ? 'Searching...' : `${count} results`)}
      </Command.Status>
      <Command.List className={styles.commandList}>
        {loading ? <Command.Loading className={styles.commandEmpty}>Fetching packages...</Command.Loading> : null}
        {loading ? null : <Command.Empty className={styles.commandEmpty}>Type to search.</Command.Empty>}
        <Results onLoading={setLoading} />
      </Command.List>
    </Command.Root>
  )
}

import * as Command from '@gentleduck/primitives/command'
import * as React from 'react'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

const FRUITS = ['apple', 'banana', 'cherry', 'grape', 'mango']

export function CommandControlledExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = React.useState('cherry')

  return (
    <div className={styles.stack}>
      <Command.Root
        className={styles.command}
        disablePointerSelection
        aria-label="Fruit"
        loop
        onValueChange={setValue}
        value={value}>
        <Command.Input className={styles.commandInput} placeholder="Search fruit..." />
        <Command.List className={styles.commandList}>
          {FRUITS.map((fruit) => (
            <Command.Item className={styles.item} key={fruit} value={fruit}>
              {fruit}
            </Command.Item>
          ))}
        </Command.List>
      </Command.Root>
      <p className={styles.note}>
        Highlighted: {value || 'nothing'}. The mouse leaves the highlight alone, and the arrow keys wrap with loop.
      </p>
    </div>
  )
}

import * as Command from '@gentleduck/primitives/command'
import * as React from 'react'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

function CreateItem({ onCreate }: { onCreate: (label: string) => void }) {
  const search = Command.useCommandSearch()
  if (!search) return null
  return (
    <Command.Item className={styles.item} forceMount onSelect={() => onCreate(search)} value={`create ${search}`}>
      Create label "{search}"
    </Command.Item>
  )
}

export function CommandCreateItemExample() {
  const [labels, setLabels] = React.useState(['bug', 'feature', 'docs'])

  return (
    <Command.Root className={styles.command} aria-label="Labels">
      <Command.Input className={styles.commandInput} placeholder="Find or create a label..." />
      <Command.List className={styles.commandList}>
        <Command.Empty className={styles.commandEmpty}>No label matches.</Command.Empty>
        {labels.map((label) => (
          <Command.Item className={styles.item} key={label} value={label}>
            {label}
          </Command.Item>
        ))}
        <CreateItem onCreate={(label) => setLabels((current) => [...current, label])} />
      </Command.List>
    </Command.Root>
  )
}

import * as Command from '@gentleduck/primitives/command'
import * as React from 'react'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

const ROWS = Array.from({ length: 5000 }, (_, index) => `Row ${index + 1}`)
const ROW = 32
const VIEW = 256

export function CommandVirtualExample() {
  const view = React.useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
  const [top, setTop] = React.useState(0)
  const first = Math.max(0, Math.floor(top / ROW) - 3)
  const last = Math.min(ROWS.length, Math.ceil((top + VIEW) / ROW) + 3)
  const scrollToIndex = React.useCallback((index: number) => {
    const box = view.current
    if (!box) return
    if (index * ROW < box.scrollTop) box.scrollTop = index * ROW
    else if ((index + 1) * ROW > box.scrollTop + VIEW) box.scrollTop = (index + 1) * ROW - VIEW
  }, [])

  return (
    <Command.Root className={styles.command} aria-label="Rows" shouldFilter={false}>
      <Command.Input className={styles.commandInput} placeholder="Arrow through 5,000 rows..." />
      <div
        onScroll={(event) => setTop(event.currentTarget.scrollTop)}
        ref={view}
        style={{ height: VIEW, overflow: 'auto' }}>
        <Command.List
          style={{ height: ROWS.length * ROW, position: 'relative' }}
          virtual={{ count: ROWS.length, scrollToIndex }}>
          {ROWS.slice(first, last).map((row, offset) => (
            <Command.Item
              className={styles.item}
              index={first + offset}
              key={row}
              style={{ height: ROW, insetInline: 0, position: 'absolute', top: (first + offset) * ROW }}
              value={row}>
              {row}
            </Command.Item>
          ))}
        </Command.List>
      </div>
    </Command.Root>
  )
}

import * as Command from '@gentleduck/primitives/command'
import * as Dialog from '@gentleduck/primitives/dialog'
import * as React from 'react'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

export function CommandDialogExample() {
  const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false)

  React.useEffect(() => {
    const onKey = (event: KeyboardEvent) => {
      if (event.key === 'k' && (event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey)) {
        event.preventDefault()
        setOpen((value) => !value)
      }
    }
    document.addEventListener('keydown', onKey)
    return () => document.removeEventListener('keydown', onKey)
  }, [])

  return (
    <Dialog.Root onOpenChange={setOpen} open={open}>
      <Dialog.Trigger className={styles.button}>Open with Ctrl K</Dialog.Trigger>
      <Dialog.Portal>
        <Dialog.Overlay className={`${styles.overlay} ${styles.fade}`} />
        <Dialog.Content aria-describedby={undefined} className={styles.dialog} style={{ padding: 0 }}>
          <Dialog.Title className={styles.title} style={{ padding: '0.75rem 0.75rem 0' }}>
            Jump to
          </Dialog.Title>
          <Command.Root className={styles.command} aria-label="Jump to" style={{ border: 0, width: '100%' }}>
            <Command.Input className={styles.commandInput} placeholder="Search pages..." />
            <Command.List className={styles.commandList}>
              <Command.Empty className={styles.commandEmpty}>No page found.</Command.Empty>
              {['Dashboard', 'Projects', 'Team', 'Settings'].map((page) => (
                <Command.Item className={styles.item} key={page} onSelect={() => setOpen(false)} value={page}>
                  {page}
                </Command.Item>
              ))}
            </Command.List>
          </Command.Root>
        </Dialog.Content>
      </Dialog.Portal>
    </Dialog.Root>
  )
}

A `filter` replaces that test with a score: `0` hides an item, and a higher score puts it before a lower one. ```tsx function score(text: string, search: string, keywords: string[]) { const word = text.toLowerCase() const query = search.toLowerCase() if (word.startsWith(query)) return 1 if (word.includes(query) || keywords.some((keyword) => keyword.includes(query))) return 0.5 return 0 } ... ``` `fuzzyFilter` is a ready-made `filter` that finds an item by the letters of the search in order, so "apl" finds "Apple", ignoring case and accents. It ranks a match at the start of the text first, then one at the start of a word, then letters side by side, and a shorter text over a longer one, as cmdk's default scoring does. It is opt-in, so a command that does not import it does not ship it. ```tsx ... ``` `limit` caps how many matches the list shows, the best ranked first, as in Base UI. A `forceMount` item shows beside them. ```tsx ... ``` Items and groups trade the places they hold among their parent's children, so a heading, a separator or `Command.Empty` stays where it is, and a group moves by its best item. Once the search is cleared every item is back in its own place, including one added while the search was on. An item that mounts, unmounts or changes its text, `value`, `keywords` or `disabled` is filtered at once, without waiting for the next keystroke. With `shouldFilter={false}` the command filters nothing and you render the matches yourself, reading the search with `useCommandSearch`. `Command.Empty` then shows once you render no item. ```tsx function Results() { const search = Command.useCommandSearch() const { data = [] } = useSearch(search) return data.map((hit) => ( {hit.title} )) } No results ``` ## Highlight The first visible item is highlighted on mount and after every keystroke. `defaultValue` names the item highlighted first instead. `value` and `onValueChange` control the highlight by the items' `value`: the command asks for a change and moves only once you pass it back. An empty string highlights nothing. ```tsx const [value, setValue] = React.useState('profile') ... ``` Moving the highlight renders nothing: the command writes `data-highlighted` and `aria-selected` on the item, and the input's `aria-activedescendant`, straight to the DOM. `disablePointerSelection` leaves the highlight where it is as the mouse moves over the items, as in cmdk. A click still selects. ## Loading and the result count `Command.Loading` marks the list as loading while its items are fetched, as in cmdk. It is a `progressbar` named "Loading", and `progress`, from 0 to 100, sets how far it has come. `Command.Status` announces how many items match, as Base UI's `Combobox.Status` does. It is a polite, atomic `status` region, and its children can be a function of the count. Hide it with a class such as `sr-only` to keep it for a screen reader alone. ```tsx {loading && Searching...} {(count) => `${count} results`} ... ``` ## Animating the list's height `Command.List` writes the height of the rows it shows to `--gentleduck-command-list-height` whenever a search, an added item or a resize changes it, as cmdk does with `--cmdk-list-height`. It measures the rows, not the list, so the list's own height can follow it: ```css [data-slot='command-list'] { height: var(--gentleduck-command-list-height); transition: height 150ms ease; } ``` A DOM with no `ResizeObserver`, such as a test's, leaves it unset. ## Virtual lists `virtual` on `Command.List` takes `{ count, scrollToIndex }` for a list that draws only some of its items, as a virtualizer such as TanStack Virtual does. {virtualizer.getVirtualItems().map((row) => ( {rows[row.index]} ))}

Off with `vimBindings={false}` | | `Alt+ArrowDown` | Highlights the first item of the next group, as in cmdk. {FRUITS.map((fruit) => ( {fruit} ))}

) } ``` ### A create item ```tsx 'use client' import * as Command from '@gentleduck/primitives/command' import * as React from 'react' import styles from '../primitives.module.css' function CreateItem({ onCreate }: { onCreate: (label: string) => void }) { const search = Command.useCommandSearch() if (!search) return null return ( onCreate(search)} value={`create ${search}`}> Create label "{search}" ) } export function CommandCreateItemExample() { const [labels, setLabels] = React.useState(['bug', 'feature', 'docs']) return ( No label matches. {labels.map((label) => ( {label} ))} setLabels((current) => [...current, label])} /> ) } ``` ### Disabled items ```tsx 'use client' import * as Command from '@gentleduck/primitives/command' import styles from '../primitives.module.css' export function CommandDisabledItemsExample() { return ( PDF Word (needs a paid plan) CSV ) } ``` ### Virtual list ```tsx 'use client' import * as Command from '@gentleduck/primitives/command' import * as React from 'react' import styles from '../primitives.module.css' const ROWS = Array.from({ length: 5000 }, (_, index) => `Row ${index + 1}`) const ROW = 32 const VIEW = 256 export function CommandVirtualExample() { const view = React.useRef(null) const [top, setTop] = React.useState(0) const first = Math.max(0, Math.floor(top / ROW) - 3) const last = Math.min(ROWS.length, Math.ceil((top + VIEW) / ROW) + 3) const scrollToIndex = React.useCallback((index: number) => { const box = view.current if (!box) return if (index * ROW < box.scrollTop) box.scrollTop = index * ROW else if ((index + 1) * ROW > box.scrollTop + VIEW) box.scrollTop = (index + 1) * ROW - VIEW }, []) return (

Off with `vimBindings={false}` | | `Ctrl+P` / `Ctrl+K` | Highlights the previous enabled item, as in cmdk. Off with `vimBindings={false}` | | `Alt+ArrowDown` | Highlights the first item of the next group, as in cmdk. Items outside a group count as one group | | `Alt+ArrowUp` | Highlights the first item of the highlighted one's group, or of the group before from there | | `Meta+ArrowDown` / `Meta+ArrowUp` | Highlights the last or first enabled item, as in cmdk | | `Home` / `End` | Highlights the first or last enabled item | | `PageDown` / `PageUp` | Moves a page, the height of the nearest box that scrolls the items, or to the last or first item when nothing scrolls, as in React Aria | | `Enter` | Selects the highlighted item by clicking it, so an item rendered as a link follows it. A button, link or field inside the command keeps its own `Enter` | | `Space` | Selects the focused item | | `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Leaves the command, as from any field, so a keyboard user can get past an inline palette. A dialog around it still keeps focus inside the dialog | While an input method is composing text, the command leaves every key to it, so the `Enter` that confirms a word selects nothing. `. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `dir` | `'ltr' \| 'rtl'` | - | Text direction, written on the root alone; the parts inherit it | | `shouldFilter` | `boolean` | `true` | Filters the items by the search. A `forceMount` item shows beside them | | `value` | `string` | - | The `value` of the highlighted item, to control the highlight. `''` highlights nothing | | `defaultValue` | `string` | - | The `value` of the item highlighted first | | `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | - | Called with the `value` of the item the highlight moves to, or `''` when it leaves every item | | `asChild` | `boolean` | - | Render as child element | ### `Command.Input` The search input field. Renders an `` that names the highlighted option in `aria-activedescendant`, so a screen reader announces it as the arrow keys move. A controlled `value` filters the list whenever it changes, including when the consumer clears it, and only by the value the owner commits, so an edit the owner refuses does not filter the list on text the input does not show. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `asChild` | `boolean` | - | Render as child element | Accepts all standard HTML input attributes. ### `Command.List` Container for items and groups. Renders a `
    `. Handles internal filtering and item visibility based on the search value, and writes the height of the rows it shows to `--gentleduck-command-list-height`. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `virtual` | `{ count: number; scrollToIndex: (index: number) => void }` | - | Draws only some of the items, as a virtualizer does. `count` is how many the whole list holds, and `scrollToIndex` brings one into the DOM | | `asChild` | `boolean` | - | Render as child element | ### `Command.Item` A selectable item within the list. Renders a `
  • `. A mouse selects it on pointer up and a touch on the click. A click with no pointer behind it, such as a screen reader's, selects it too. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `value` | `string` | - | Item value passed to `onSelect` | | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables the item | | `textValue` | `string` | - | Text for search matching (auto-derived from text content if not provided) | | `keywords` | `string[]` | - | More words a search matches the item by, such as aliases, as in cmdk | | `forceMount` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows the item whatever the search, such as a "Create" item. It is no match, so `Command.Empty` can show beside it | | `index` | `number` | - | The item's place in a `virtual` list, from 0, written as `aria-posinset` | | `onSelect` | `(value: string) => void` | - | Called when the item is selected | | `asChild` | `boolean` | - | Render as child element | ### `Command.Group` Groups items with an optional heading. Renders a `
    `. A group is hidden when none of its items match the search. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `heading` | `React.ReactNode` | - | Optional group heading | | `forceMount` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows the group and its heading whatever the search | | `asChild` | `boolean` | - | Render as child element | ### `Command.Empty` Shows when no item matches the search, or when there is no item at all. A `forceMount` item is no match, so it does not hide it. Renders a `
    `. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `asChild` | `boolean` | - | Render as child element | ### `Command.Loading` Marks the list as loading. Renders a `
    ` with `role="progressbar"`, named "Loading". | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `progress` | `number` | - | How far the loading has come, from 0 to 100. Left out, the bar shows no amount | | `asChild` | `boolean` | - | Render as child element | ### `Command.Status` Announces how many items match. Renders a `
    ` with `role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"` and `aria-atomic`. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `children` | `React.ReactNode \| ((count: number) => React.ReactNode)` | - | What to announce, or a function of the count that returns it | | `asChild` | `boolean` | - | Render as child element | ### `Command.Separator` A visual separator between groups. Renders a `
    `. Hidden when adjacent groups have no visible items. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `asChild` | `boolean` | - | Render as child element | *** ## Hooks ### `useCommandSearch()` Returns the text typed into `Command.Input`. Use it to render your own matches under `shouldFilter={false}`, or to show the search elsewhere in the command. ```tsx const search = Command.useCommandSearch() ``` ### `useCommandState(selector)` Reads the command's state and renders again only when what `selector` picks from it changes, as in cmdk. The state is `search`, the text typed; `value`, the highlighted item's `value` or `''`; and `count`, how many items match and show, after `limit`. What the selector returns is kept until the state changes, so a selector that builds an object does not render again on every read. ```tsx const count = Command.useCommandState((state) => state.count) const highlighted = Command.useCommandState((state) => state.value) ``` ### `useCommandContext(consumerName, scope)` The internals the parts share: the input's ref, the highlighted item's ref, and `highlight(item)` to move the highlight. Building a part of your own is its one use; read the search with `useCommandSearch`.

Picking a radio fires the form's `change` event once, as a native radio does. Resetting the form puts back the value the group started with and fires nothing. ### `RadioGroup.Item` A single radio control. Renders a `button` with `role="radio"`, and inside a form a hidden `` beside it. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `value` | `string` | (required) | Unique value for the item | | `textValue` | `string` | - | Text typeahead matches. Falls back to `aria-label`, then the item's text | | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables this item | | `...props` | `React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'button'>` | - | Additional props for the radio button element | Exposes `data-state` (`checked` / `unchecked`), `data-disabled`, `data-readonly` and `data-value`. Items take their direction from the group and carry no `dir` of their own. ### `RadioGroup.ItemProvider` / `RadioGroup.ItemTrigger` / `RadioGroup.ItemBubbleInput` `RadioGroup.Item` is `RadioGroup.ItemTrigger` inside a `RadioGroup.ItemProvider`, with a `RadioGroup.ItemBubbleInput` beside it when the group has a `name`. Compose the three yourself to place the hidden input, give it props of its own, or render it without a `name`. ```tsx ``` `RadioGroup.ItemProvider` takes the item's `value` and `disabled`. `RadioGroup.ItemTrigger` takes the props of `RadioGroup.Item` except those two. `RadioGroup.ItemBubbleInput` takes the props of an ``; its `name`, `value`, `checked`, `required`, `disabled` and `form` come from the group and the item. Focus given to it, as when a form refuses an empty submit to a required group, moves to the item's radio. ### `RadioGroup.Indicator` Indicator content that mounts when the parent item is checked. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `forceMount` | `true` | - | Force indicator to stay mounted for animation control | | `...props` | `React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'span'>` | - | Additional props for the indicator element | ## Keyboard interactions | Key | Action | | --- | --- | | ArrowUp / ArrowLeft | Move focus to previous item and select it | | ArrowDown / ArrowRight | Move focus to next item and select it | | Home / PageUp | Move to first item and select it | | End / PageDown | Move to last item and select it | | a-z | Move to the next item after the focused one whose text starts with it, and select it. It matches `textValue`, then `aria-label`, then the text, skips a nested group's radios and a hidden one, and typing the focused radio's name keeps focus on it | | g g | Jump to first item and select it | | Shift+g (`G`) | Jump to last item and select it | | Space | Select focused item | | Enter | Nothing, as on a native radio | In a `readOnly` group these keys move focus without selecting.

import * as ToggleGroup from '@gentleduck/primitives/toggle-group'
import * as React from 'react'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

export function ToggleGroupMultipleExample() {
  const [marks, setMarks] = React.useState<string[]>(['bold'])

  return (
    <div className={styles.stack}>
      <ToggleGroup.Root
        aria-label="Formatting"
        className={styles.group}
        onValueChange={setMarks}
        type="multiple"
        value={marks}>
        {['bold', 'italic', 'underline'].map((value) => (
          <ToggleGroup.Item className={styles.toggle} key={value} value={value}>
            {value}
          </ToggleGroup.Item>
        ))}
      </ToggleGroup.Root>
      <p className={styles.note}>On: {marks.join(', ') || 'none'}</p>
    </div>

import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

export function ToggleGroupNoRovingExample() {
  return (
    <div className={styles.stack}>
      <ToggleGroup.Root aria-label="Filters" className={styles.group} rovingFocus={false} type="multiple">
        {['open', 'closed', 'draft'].map((value) => (

            {value}

        ))}
      </ToggleGroup.Root>
      <p className={styles.note}>rovingFocus off makes every item its own Tab stop.</p>
    </div>
  )
}

Content
 ``` }> When `present` changes from `true` to `false`, Presence waits for the CSS animations the child runs as it closes to end before unmounting. No JavaScript animation library needed. ## Examples ### An exit animation ```tsx 'use client' import { Presence } from '@gentleduck/primitives/presence' import * as React from 'react' import styles from '../primitives.module.css' export function PresenceExitAnimationExample() { const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(true) return (
Stays in the page until its fade out ends.
) } ``` ### A render function ```tsx 'use client' import { Presence } from '@gentleduck/primitives/presence' import * as React from 'react' import styles from '../primitives.module.css' export function PresenceRenderFunctionExample() { const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(true) return (
{({ present }) => (
The child reads present itself while it animates out.
)}
) } ``` *** ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `present` | `boolean` | - | Whether the child should be mounted | | `children` | `ReactElement \| ((props: { present: boolean }) => ReactElement)` | - | Child element or render function | ## Exit animations Presence reads the child's computed `animation-name` as it closes. When it differs from the one the child opened with, Presence waits on the `finished` promise of every CSS animation `element.getAnimations()` lists on the child itself: * Several exit animations hold the content until the last of them ends. * An animation that is cancelled, whether by a style change or by the content being hidden or removed, counts as ended, even when it is cancelled in the frame it starts and the browser sends no `animationcancel`. * A paused animation holds the content until it plays again and ends. One that repeats forever holds it for good. * A name with no `@keyframes`, content hidden with `display: none`, and the animation it opened with still set on close all leave nothing to wait for, so the content unmounts at once. * CSS transitions, animations made with `element.animate()` and animations on the child's descendants are not waited for. Where the browser has no `element.getAnimations()`, as in jsdom, the content unmounts at once. A test that plays an exit stubs `getAnimations` with an animation whose `finished` promise it settles. ## The child's ref Presence puts its own ref on the child beside the child's, through one ref that keeps its identity for as long as the node lives. React calls the child's ref once when the node mounts and once when it goes, however often the child renders with a new ref, so an inline callback ref that sets state on attach does not loop. A ref the child takes on after mounting is the one told when the node goes, and a cleanup a callback ref returns runs then. ## Render function form For more control, use a render function: ```tsx {({ present }) => (
Content
)} ``` ## State machine }> Presence uses three states: `mounted` (in the page), `exiting` (playing its exit animation) and `unmounted` (removed). Content mounts in the same render that sets `present`, and Presence reads the child's styles only when it closes, to tell an exit animation from the one that ran while it was open.

```tsx
import * as Menu from '@gentleduck/primitives/menu'
```

<Callout icon={<Lightbulb />}>
  Menu is the **base primitive** that Context Menu and Menubar build on top of. It provides the full menu system without a trigger mechanism.
</Callout>

The anatomy and API are identical to Context Menu's content-level components. See [Context Menu](/duck-primitives/api/context-menu) for the full component list.

Menu does not include a trigger mechanism. Context Menu adds right-click triggering; Menubar adds click-on-menu-title triggering. Use Menu directly when building custom trigger mechanisms.

`Menu.Anchor` is the element the content is placed against, and takes `virtualRef`, as [`Popper.Anchor`](/duck-primitives/api/popper) does, to open at a point such as the pointer. `Menu.Portal` takes `container` and `forceMount`.

***

## Examples

### A trigger of your own

<ComponentPreview name="menu-anchor" description="Menu has no trigger, so an Anchor and the open state make one, as DropdownMenu does.">
```tsx
'use client'

import * as Menu from '@gentleduck/primitives/menu'
import * as React from 'react'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

export function MenuAnchorExample() {
  const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false)

  return (
    <Menu.Root modal={false} onOpenChange={setOpen} open={open}>
      <Menu.Anchor asChild>
        <button
          aria-expanded={open}
          aria-haspopup="menu"
          className={styles.button}
          onKeyDown={(event) => {
            if (!['Enter', ' ', 'ArrowDown'].includes(event.key)) return
            event.preventDefault()
            setOpen(true)
          }}
          onPointerDown={(event) => {
            if (event.button !== 0 || event.ctrlKey) return
            setOpen(!open)
            if (!open) event.preventDefault()
          }}
          type="button">
          A trigger of your own
        </button>
      </Menu.Anchor>
      <Menu.Portal>
        <Menu.Content align="start" className={styles.content} sideOffset={6}>
          <Menu.Item className={styles.item}>New tab</Menu.Item>
          <Menu.Item className={styles.item}>New window</Menu.Item>
          <Menu.Separator className={styles.separator} />
          <Menu.Item className={styles.item}>Close</Menu.Item>
        </Menu.Content>
      </Menu.Portal>
    </Menu.Root>
  )
}

```
</ComponentPreview>

### Opened by a shortcut

<ComponentPreview name="menu-shortcut-trigger" description="A keyboard shortcut opens the menu at an anchor that is not a button.">
```tsx
'use client'

import * as Menu from '@gentleduck/primitives/menu'
import * as React from 'react'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

export function MenuShortcutTriggerExample() {
  const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false)

  React.useEffect(() => {
    const onKey = (event: KeyboardEvent) => {
      if (event.key === '.' && (event.ctrlKey || event.metaKey)) {
        event.preventDefault()
        setOpen(true)
      }
    }
    document.addEventListener('keydown', onKey)
    return () => document.removeEventListener('keydown', onKey)
  }, [])

  return (
    <Menu.Root onOpenChange={setOpen} open={open}>
      <Menu.Anchor className={styles.box}>Press Ctrl . to open the quick actions here</Menu.Anchor>
      <Menu.Portal>
        <Menu.Content className={styles.content} sideOffset={6}>
          <Menu.Item className={styles.item}>Quick fix</Menu.Item>
          <Menu.Item className={styles.item}>Rename symbol</Menu.Item>
        </Menu.Content>
      </Menu.Portal>
    </Menu.Root>
  )
}

```
</ComponentPreview>

***

## API

### `Menu.Root`

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | `boolean` | - | Controlled open state |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` | - | Called on state change |
| `dir` | `'ltr' \| 'rtl'` | - | Reading direction for keyboard navigation |
| `modal` | `boolean` | `true` | Enable modal behavior |

## Sub-components

`Menu.Anchor`, `Menu.Portal`, `Menu.Content`, `Menu.Group`, `Menu.Label`, `Menu.Item`, `Menu.CheckboxItem`, `Menu.RadioGroup`, `Menu.RadioItem`, `Menu.ItemIndicator`, `Menu.Separator`, `Menu.Arrow`, `Menu.Sub`, `Menu.SubTrigger`, `Menu.SubContent`

<Callout icon={<Target />}>
  All sub-components also export short aliases: `Root`, `Anchor`, `Portal`, `Content`, etc.
</Callout>

import * as Menubar from '@gentleduck/primitives/menubar'
import * as React from 'react'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

export function MenubarBasicExample() {
  const [wrap, setWrap] = React.useState(true)
  const [theme, setTheme] = React.useState('system')

  return (
    <Menubar.Root className={styles.menubar}>
      <Menubar.Menu value="file">
        <Menubar.Trigger className={styles.menubarTrigger}>File</Menubar.Trigger>
        <Menubar.Portal>
          <Menubar.Content className={styles.content} sideOffset={6}>
            <Menubar.Item className={styles.item}>
              New file <span className={styles.shortcut}>Ctrl N</span>
            </Menubar.Item>
            <Menubar.Sub>
              <Menubar.SubTrigger className={styles.item}>
                Open recent <span className={styles.shortcut}>{'>'}</span>
              </Menubar.SubTrigger>
              <Menubar.Portal>
                <Menubar.SubContent className={styles.content}>
                  <Menubar.Item className={styles.item}>notes.md</Menubar.Item>
                  <Menubar.Item className={styles.item}>budget.csv</Menubar.Item>
                </Menubar.SubContent>
              </Menubar.Portal>
            </Menubar.Sub>
            <Menubar.Separator className={styles.separator} />
            <Menubar.Item className={styles.item} disabled>
              Print
            </Menubar.Item>
          </Menubar.Content>
        </Menubar.Portal>
      </Menubar.Menu>
      <Menubar.Menu value="view">
        <Menubar.Trigger className={styles.menubarTrigger}>View</Menubar.Trigger>
        <Menubar.Portal>
          <Menubar.Content className={styles.content} sideOffset={6}>
            <Menubar.CheckboxItem checked={wrap} className={styles.item} onCheckedChange={setWrap}>
              <span className={styles.itemIndicator}>
                <Menubar.ItemIndicator>x</Menubar.ItemIndicator>
              </span>
              Word wrap
            </Menubar.CheckboxItem>
            <Menubar.Separator className={styles.separator} />
            <Menubar.Label className={styles.groupLabel}>Theme</Menubar.Label>
            <Menubar.RadioGroup onValueChange={setTheme} value={theme}>
              {['light', 'dark', 'system'].map((value) => (
                <Menubar.RadioItem className={styles.item} key={value} value={value}>
                  <span className={styles.itemIndicator}>
                    <Menubar.ItemIndicator>o</Menubar.ItemIndicator>
                  </span>
                  {value}
                </Menubar.RadioItem>
              ))}
            </Menubar.RadioGroup>
          </Menubar.Content>
        </Menubar.Portal>
      </Menubar.Menu>
    </Menubar.Root>
  )
}

export function MenubarVerticalExample() {
  return (

      {['Projects', 'Team', 'Settings'].map((menu) => (

              <Menubar.Item className={styles.item}>Manage</Menubar.Item>
            </Menubar.Content>
          </Menubar.Portal>
        </Menubar.Menu>
      ))}
    </Menubar.Root>
  )
}

import * as Menubar from '@gentleduck/primitives/menubar'
import * as React from 'react'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

export function MenubarControlledExample() {
  const [value, setValue] = React.useState('')

  return (
    <div className={styles.stack}>
      <Menubar.Root className={styles.menubar} onValueChange={setValue} value={value}>
        {['Edit', 'Selection', 'Help'].map((menu) => (
          <Menubar.Menu key={menu} value={menu}>
            <Menubar.Trigger className={styles.menubarTrigger}>{menu}</Menubar.Trigger>
            <Menubar.Portal>
              <Menubar.Content className={styles.content} sideOffset={6}>
                <Menubar.Item className={styles.item}>{menu} item</Menubar.Item>
              </Menubar.Content>
            </Menubar.Portal>
          </Menubar.Menu>
        ))}
      </Menubar.Root>
      <div className={styles.row}>
        <button className={styles.button} onClick={() => setValue('Help')} type="button">
          Open Help
        </button>
        <button className={styles.button} onClick={() => setValue('')} type="button">
          Close
        </button>
      </div>
      <p className={styles.note}>
        Open menu: {value || 'none'}. While one is open, the pointer moving across opens the next.
      </p>
    </div>
  )
}

import * as Menubar from '@gentleduck/primitives/menubar'
import * as React from 'react'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

export function MenubarModalExample() {
  const [modal, setModal] = React.useState(true)

  return (
    <div className={styles.stack}>
      <label className={styles.choice}>
        <input checked={modal} onChange={(event) => setModal(event.target.checked)} type="checkbox" />
        modal
      </label>
      <Menubar.Root className={styles.menubar} modal={modal}>
        <Menubar.Menu value="file">
          <Menubar.Trigger className={styles.menubarTrigger}>File</Menubar.Trigger>
          <Menubar.Portal>
            <Menubar.Content className={styles.content} sideOffset={6}>
              <Menubar.Item className={styles.item}>Save</Menubar.Item>
            </Menubar.Content>
          </Menubar.Portal>
        </Menubar.Menu>
      </Menubar.Root>
      <p className={styles.note}>
        Modal locks the page's scroll and keeps focus in the open menu. Off, the page stays usable.
      </p>
    </div>
  )
}

import * as Menubar from '@gentleduck/primitives/menubar'
import * as React from 'react'
import styles from '../primitives.module.css'

export function MenubarDisabledExample() {
  const [disabled, setDisabled] = React.useState(true)

  return (
    <div className={styles.stack}>
      <Menubar.Root className={styles.menubar} disabled={disabled}>
        {['File', 'Edit'].map((menu) => (
          <Menubar.Menu key={menu} value={menu}>
            <Menubar.Trigger className={styles.menubarTrigger}>{menu}</Menubar.Trigger>
            <Menubar.Portal>
              <Menubar.Content className={styles.content} sideOffset={6}>
                <Menubar.Item className={styles.item}>{menu} item</Menubar.Item>
              </Menubar.Content>
            </Menubar.Portal>
          </Menubar.Menu>
        ))}
      </Menubar.Root>
      <button className={styles.button} onClick={() => setDisabled((value) => !value)} type="button">
        {disabled ? 'Enable the bar' : 'Disable the bar'}
      </button>
    </div>
  )
}

It is in the page from the first render, the server's HTML included, so the download starts before the page hydrates. Until it loads it is hidden but still laid out, so `loading="lazy"` still waits for the viewport. An image that loads as 0 by 0 counts as an error. The trapped scope lets focus into the portalled panel, its branch, and back.

) } ``` *** ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `trapped` | `boolean` | `false` | Trap focus inside the scope | | `loop` | `boolean` | `false` | Tab wraps from last to first element | | `asChild` | `boolean` | `false` | Render as child element | | `onMountAutoFocus` | `(event) => void` | - | Called when focus moves in on mount. Prevent default to skip auto-focus. | | `onUnmountAutoFocus` | `(event) => void` | - | Called when focus restores on unmount | | `branches` | `readonly HTMLElement[]` | - | Nodes outside the scope's DOM, such as a nested layer's portalled content, that focus may move into | Focus that lands in an input selects its text, on mount and when focus comes back to it. A Tab pressed while an input method is composing text is left to the input method. An `onKeyDown` passed to the scope runs before its own handler, and a Tab it prevents does not loop. A looping scope counts a group of native radios as one stop, as the browser does: Tab leaves the group from any radio in it, and looping into the group lands on its checked radio. A focusable `svg` is a stop, and mount focus passes over a link inside an `svg` as it does an html one. Nothing inside a `hidden` or `inert` element or a disabled `
` is a stop. The walk for stops enters each open shadow root inside the scope and follows its slots, so a field inside a custom element at the scope's edge is its first or last stop, and radios in a shadow root are a group apart from those of the same name outside it. A Tab the browser would take to a positive `tabIndex` outside a trapped scope lands on the next stop inside it, read in the scope's own order, and a Shift+Tab on the one before. A trapped scope whose last focused element has gone, such as a button in a branch that closed, takes focus to its own element when focus leaves. ## Iframes, shadow roots and a changing element The scope works in its container's own document, so inside an iframe it traps, loops and gives focus back there. It reads the element focused inside each open shadow root, so it works inside a shadow root too, and a trapped scope holding a custom element gives focus back to the field inside it rather than to the element itself. A scope whose element changes, as with `asChild` when its child changes type, stays the same scope. It gives focus back once, when it unmounts, to what had focus when it first mounted, and a scope opened over another keeps the one under it paused throughout. ## Branches A trapped scope keeps focus inside its own DOM, so a nested layer portalled out of it, such as a popover's content, needs to register as a branch. Host the branches with `useFocusScopeBranchRegistry` and `FocusScopeBranchProvider`, and register each node with `useFocusScopeBranch`: ```tsx import { FocusScope, FocusScopeBranchProvider, useFocusScopeBranch, useFocusScopeBranchRegistry, } from '@gentleduck/primitives/focus-scope' function Panel({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) { const { nodes, registry } = useFocusScopeBranchRegistry() return (
{children}
 ) } function Portalled() { const [node, setNode] = React.useState(null) useFocusScopeBranch(node) return createPortal(
...
, document.body) } ``` A modal `Dialog` and a modal `Popover` host branches, and `Popover.Content` registers itself, so a popover inside a dialog needs nothing extra. }> Used internally by the content of Dialog, Popover, Select and every menu, and a Tooltip's content registers as a branch. You typically don't need to use it directly unless building your own overlay components.
